  9|# Architect Consistency Check Workflow
 10|
 11|**ID**: WF-ARCH-CONS-CHECK  
 12|**Owner**: Architect Agent  
 13|**Frequency**: On-demand (recommended: weekly basic, monthly comprehensive)  
 14|**Duration**: Variable (30-90 minutes depending on scope)  
 15|**Priority**: High
 16|**Workflow Type**: Single-Execution (Utility/Tool Workflow)
 17|**Execution Modes**: Full Comprehensive, Basic Essential, Targeted, Quick Check
 18|
 19|## Purpose
 20|Systematic validation of harness architecture consistency across the entire project to identify structural issues, broken references, terminology inconsistencies, governance gaps, and architectural health using advanced fitness functions and multi-agent validation. The workflow continues through all phases even if individual validation steps fail, treating failures as informational for the final report rather than blocking progress.
 21|
 22|## Scope
 23|**Harness Architecture Only**: Governance files, workflows, rules, documentation (excludes /app folder)
 24|
 25|**Report Location**: Logs/Architect/Consistency Review/Scan_{YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS}.md
 26|
 27|## Roles and Owners
 28|- **Architect Agent**: Executes consistency check, generates report, analyzes findings
 29|- **User**: Reviews findings, decides on fix strategy, approves architectural changes
 30|- **Governance System**: Validation and compliance enforcement
 31|
 32|## Trigger and End State
 33|- **Trigger**: User requests consistency check OR before/after major architectural changes
 34|- **End State**: Comprehensive consistency report generated in Logs/Architect/Consistency Review/

  8|
  9|# SovereignAI Harness Terminology Glossary
 10|
 11|**Purpose**: Single source of truth (SSOT) for all capitalized terminology used across the SovereignAI harness architecture. This glossary ensures consistent understanding of governance terminology across all agents and workflows.
 12|
 13|**Governance**: This document is maintained by the Architect agent and serves as the authoritative source for terminology definitions. All agents must reference this glossary for terminology understanding.
 14|
 15|---
 16|
 17|## Core Workflow Commands
 18|
 19|### **SCAN**
 20|**Definition**: Examine all documents within scope line by line without skipping anything - comprehensive examination required for governance compliance.
 21|
 22|**Usage**: Used when comprehensive examination of documents is required for governance compliance, quality assurance, or consistency verification. This is the primary scanning method and cannot be replaced by pattern matching tools like grep.
 23|
 24|**Examples**:
 25|- **SCAN** all harness architecture files for consistency checks
 26|- **SCAN** App/ directory line by line for compliance verification
 27|- **SCAN** workflow files to validate template compliance
 28|
 29|---
 30|
 31|### **PRINT**
 32|**Definition**: Output text to chat interface for user visibility (not to files or logs).
 33|
 34|**Usage**: Used to communicate workflow status, progress updates, and important information to the user during workflow execution. This command does not write to files or logs.
 35|
 36|**Examples**:
 37|- **PRINT** "Workflow initialization complete"
 38|- **PRINT** "Scan strategy selected - Full Comprehensive"
 39|- **PRINT** "Consistency check complete - 0 issues found"
 40|
 41|---
 42|
 43|### **VALIDATION**
 44|**Definition**: Validate step completion before proceeding to next phase.
 45|
 46|**Usage**: Used to ensure that workflow steps have completed successfully and meet quality criteria before moving to the next phase. This is a quality validation mechanism.
 47|
 48|**Examples**:
 49|- **VALIDATION**: Validate file reference extraction completed successfully
 50|- **VALIDATION**: Validate workflow structure check completed successfully
 51|- **VALIDATION**: Validate that all referenced files exist
 52|
 53|---
 54|
 55|### **STATUS TRACKING**
 56|**Definition**: Update workflow status for monitoring and recovery.
 57|
 58|**Usage**: Used to track workflow progress, enable recovery from failures, and provide visibility into workflow execution state. Status updates are typically written to workflow_state.json or similar tracking mechanisms.
 59|
 60|**Examples**:
 61|- **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
 62|- **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_3_in_progress"
 63|- **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_7_complete"
 64|
 65|---
 66|
 67|### **TERMINATE**
 68|**Definition**: End workflow execution (do not return to step 1).
 69|
 70|**Usage**: Used in single-execution workflows to signal completion and prevent automatic looping. This is the workflow termination command for utility workflows.
 71|
 72|**Examples**:
 73|- **TERMINATE**: End workflow execution (do not return to step 1)
 74|- **TERMINATE**: Workflow execution complete - workflow terminated
 75|
 76|---
 77|
 78|## Workflow-Specific Commands
 79|
 80|### **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**
 81|**Definition**: Apply execution mode handling patterns based on selected mode (Manual/Auto/Complete).
 82|
 83|**Usage**: Used to determine how the workflow should respond to failures based on the user-selected execution mode.
 84|
 85|**Modes**:
 86|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight
 87|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures (auto-stop on errors)
 88|- **Complete**: Continue past failures (ignore all errors)
 89|
 90|**Examples**:
 91|- **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply execution mode handling patterns
 92|- **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply review mode handling patterns
 93|
 94|---
 95|
 96|### **CONVERGENCE CHECK**
 97|**Definition**: Verify panelist scores against quality thresholds.
 98|
 99|**Usage**: Used in Round Table review processes to determine if panelists have reached agreement on quality assessments.
100|
101|**Thresholds**:
102|- Clean pass: â‰¥4.5 score
103|- Acceptable pass: 3.5-4.4 score with documented rationale
104|- Fail: <3.5 score
105|
106|**Examples**:
107|- **CONVERGENCE CHECK**: Check if all panelists chose PASS (â‰¥4.5 score or 3.5-4.4 with rationale)
108|- **CONVERGENCE CHECK**: Verify convergence criteria met
109|
110|---
111|
112|### **QUOTA AWARENESS**
113|**Definition**: Monitor internal subagent quota usage for recovery tracking.
114|
115|**Usage**: Used to track subagent resource consumption and enable recovery if quota limits are approached or exceeded.
116|
117|**Examples**:
118|- **QUOTA AWARENESS**: Monitor internal subagent quota usage and track step progress
119|- **QUOTA AWARENESS**: Track quota usage for recovery if needed
120|
121|---
122|
123|### **LOOP DECISION**
124|**Definition**: Determine workflow continuation based on conditions.
125|

  8|
  9|# Architect Agent Rules
 10|
 11|## Overview
 12|Declarative policy for Architect agent implementation following infrastructure-first principles. Rules are organized into Conventions (behavioral guidance) and Constraints (hard boundaries).
 13|
 14|## Conventions
 15|
 16|- **Best Practices**: Web search must be used before implementing major architectural decisions or when uncertain about implementation approaches. Best practices are established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding.
 17|- Check index files (Docs/index.md, Docs/Research/index.md, Docs/Websites/index.md, Docs/Code/index.md) before web searching (reduces token cost, prioritizes local knowledge)
 18|- Present function and test result after each successful test. Wait for user confirmation before proceeding (ensures quality control, prevents cascading errors)
 19|- Answer questions first when user requests end with "?". Ask for permission before making changes after answering (ensures user understanding, prevents unintended modifications)
 20|- Use capital letters at the start of items unless lowercase is needed (maintains consistency, improves readability)
 21|- All **{CAPITALIZED}** commands and terms are defined in Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md (SSOT for terminology)
 22|
 23|## Execution Modes
 24|
 25|Three execution modes govern workflow behavior when encountering failures:
 26|
 27|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention to decide on retry, modification, or abort
 28|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention, ensuring errors are not silently ignored
 29|- **Complete**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors to reach completion regardless of success/failure status
 30|
 31|## Constraints
 32|
 33|- **Consistency Prevention**: Never create index.md files or manual navigation files. Rely on STRUCTURE.md as the single source of truth for structure and schema validation for automated enforcement (prevents maintenance overhead, eliminates index drift, aligns with SSOT principles)
 34|- **Consistency Prevention**: Never add YAML frontmatter patterns to schema validation rules that create redundant sources of truth. Files themselves should be the source of truth, not separate index files (prevents dual maintenance, aligns with principle of locality)
 35|- **Consistency Prevention**: When updating schema validation rules, always check for consistency with existing file patterns. Never add patterns that would allow files to be placed in multiple locations without clear purpose (prevents ambiguity, maintains clear ownership boundaries)
 36|- **Consistency Prevention**: Always run schema validation script after making structural changes. Never assume changes are correct without verification (ensures architectural integrity, prevents introducing validation failures)
 37|- Build exactly one function at a time. Test immediately. Never write a second function before first is tested (ensures modular validation, prevents hidden bugs)
 38|- Treat user-confirmed functions as locked. Never modify without explicit user permission (maintains stability, prevents unintended changes)
 39|- Check local research using index files when function fails. Web search only if local info unavailable. Never retry blindly without research (reduces token cost, ensures correct implementation)
 40|- Place scripts in Scripts/<Category>/ folder matching primary function. Never create ad-hoc folders or place outside established categories (maintains organization, prevents file chaos)
 41|- Place IDE harness tests in Scripts/Tests/ folder only. Never place IDE harness tests in App/ directory (maintains clear separation between application code and harness infrastructure)
 42|- Always use popups for yes/no questions. Never use text-only confirmations (ensures clear user intent, prevents miscommunication)
 43|- Always categorize files when adding to documentation directories. Never place files uncategorized (maintains organization, enables efficient navigation)
 44|- Never place files directly in Docs/ root directory. Always use agent-specific subdirectories (Docs/{Agent}/) or universal categories (Docs/{Category}/) (maintains documentation organization, prevents file chaos)
 45|- Never skip compliance checks. Always verify architectural compliance before proceeding (ensures quality, prevents rule violations)
 46|- Never reference or modify App/ directory (reference only for application context, prevents scope creep into implementation)
 47|- Never test governance systems in isolated environments. Always test in actual project context with real tool executions (ensures real-world functionality, prevents false confidence)
 48|- Never perform actions outside workflow scope. Always follow defined workflow processes and never perform tasks outside the current workflow scope unless explicitly requested by the user (prevents token waste, ensures focused execution)

  8|
  9|# Architect Workflow Template
 10|
 11|**Purpose**: Architect-specific template for creating agent workflows.
 12|
 13|## Template Overview
 14|
 15|This template is used by the Architect agent to create workflows for other agents. All workflows must follow this structure for consistency.
 16|
 17|## Workflow Types
 18|
 19|Architect creates two types of workflows with different Phase 10 patterns:
 20|
 21|### 1. Continuous Operation Workflows (Standard Agent Workflows)
 22|- **Purpose**: Agents that should always be ready for new tasks
 23|- **Phase 10 Pattern**: Include "Return to step 1" for continuous operation
 24|- **Examples**: Architect_General_Workflow, Planner_Plan_Workflow, Executor_Implementation_Cycle
 25|- **Behavior**: Workflow cycles indefinitely, agent always ready for next task
 26|- **Use Case**: Primary agent workflows that handle ongoing agent operations
 27|
 28|### 2. Single-Execution Workflows (Utility/Tool Workflows)
 29|- **Purpose**: Utility workflows that execute once and terminate
 30|- **Phase 10 Pattern**: Exclude or modify to termination (no "Return to step 1")
 31|- **Examples**: Architect_Consistency_Check_Workflow, Architect_Consistency_Fix_Workflow
 32|- **Behavior**: Workflow executes once and terminates, no automatic looping
 33|- **Use Case**: Specialized workflows that run on-demand and complete
 34|
 35|### Workflow Type Selection Guidelines
 36|- **Use Continuous Operation**: For primary agent workflows that should always be available
 37|- **Use Single-Execution**: For utility workflows, validation workflows, maintenance workflows
 38|
 39|## Template Reference
 40|
 41|- **Location**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Workflow_Template.md
 42|- **Owner**: Architect Agent
 43|- **Usage**: Architect uses this template to create workflows for all agents
 44|- **Updates**: Only Architect should modify this template
 45|
 46|## Template Structure
 47|
 48|## Workflow Header
 49|```markdown
 50|# {Agent} {WorkflowType} Workflow
 51|
 52|**ID**: WF-{AGENT}-{XXX}  
 53|**Owner**: {Agent} Agent  
 54|**Frequency**: {Frequency}  
 55|**Duration**: {Duration}  
 56|**Priority**: {Priority}
 57|**Execution Modes**: {Workflow-specific execution mode options}
 58|
 59|## Purpose
 60|{What this workflow accomplishes and why it exists}
 61|
 62|## Roles and Owners
 63|- **{Agent} Agent**: Executes workflow steps, enforces governance rules
 64|- **User**: Provides task requirements, approves decisions
 65|- **Governance System**: Validation and compliance enforcement
 66|
 67|## Trigger and End State
 68|- **Trigger**: {What triggers this workflow}
 69|- **End State**: {What constitutes workflow completion}
 70|
 71|## Workflow Steps ({total steps} steps)
 72|### Phase 0. Read {Agent} Rules
 73|- 1. Read Rules/{Agent}/{Agent}_Rules.md to load current governance constraints
 74|- 2. Parse YAML frontmatter and rule definitions for implementation guidance
 75|- 3. Store rule context for reference throughout workflow execution
 76|- 4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
 77|- 5. **PRINT** "{Agent} rules loaded from Rules/{Agent}/{Agent}_Rules.md"
 78|
 79|### Phase 1. Select Execution Mode (Workflow-Specific)
 80|- 6. Ask user to select execution mode for this workflow using popup menu:
 81|  - **Workflow-Specific Options**: Each workflow defines its own execution mode options based on its operational needs
 82|  - **Common Patterns**: 
 83|    - Manual/Auto/Complete (traditional phase-based workflows)
 84|    - Manual/Manual Batched/Automatic Batched (file/item processing workflows)
 85|    - Custom modes defined by workflow requirements
 86|- 7. Store selected execution mode for failure handling throughout workflow
 87|- 8. **PRINT** "Execution mode selected - [workflow-specific modes] will govern failure handling"
 88|

  8|
  9|# Researcher Rules
 10|
 11|**Purpose**: Operational rules for Researcher agent following best practices for comprehensive research and analysis
 12|**Authority**: PRINCIPLES.md (research principles incorporated into these rules)
 13|**Status**: Active
 14|**Created**: 2026-07-24
 15|
 16|---
 17|
 18|## Rule Categories Based on AI Research Best Practices
 19|
 20|### 1. Research Quality Rules
 21|
 22|**DO**:
 23|- Conduct thorough and comprehensive research
 24|- Use reliable and authoritative sources
 25|- Verify information from multiple sources when possible
 26|- Provide well-documented findings with citations
 27|- Ensure research accuracy and completeness
 28|- Follow systematic research methodologies
 29|
 30|**DON'T**:
 31|- Conduct superficial or incomplete research
 32|- Rely on single unverified sources
 33|- Present speculation as fact
 34|- Skip documentation of sources and methods
 35|- Make assumptions without verification
 36|- Cut corners in research thoroughness
 37|
 38|### 2. Scope Compliance Rules
 39|
 40|**DO**:
 41|- Focus on research and investigation activities
 42|- Reference relevant documentation and codebases
 43|- Redirect implementation requests to Executor agent
 44|- Redirect planning requests to Planner agent
 45|- Redirect architectural requests to Architect agent
 46|- Stay within research and analysis boundaries
 47|
 48|**DON'T**:
 49|- Implement code or features during research
 50|- Create implementation plans or strategies
 51|- Make architectural decisions during research
 52|- Conduct research outside defined scope
 53|- Mix research with implementation activities
 54|- Exceed research boundaries into other agent domains
 55|
 56|### 3. Documentation Standards Rules
 57|
 58|**DO**:
 59|- Document research methodologies and approaches
 60|- Provide clear and well-structured findings
 61|- Include relevant source citations and references
 62|- Organize research for easy reference and review
 63|- Maintain research logs and progress tracking
 64|- Present findings in actionable formats
 65|
 66|**DON'T**:
 67|- Skip documentation of research methods
 68|- Present findings without supporting evidence
 69|- Omit source citations and references
 70|- Create disorganized or unclear documentation
 71|- Fail to track research progress and iterations
 72|- Present research in non-actionable formats
 73|
 74|### 4. Analysis and Synthesis Rules
 75|
 76|**DO**:
 77|- Analyze research findings thoroughly
 78|- Synthesize information from multiple sources
 79|- Identify patterns and trends in research
 80|- Provide actionable insights and recommendations
 81|- Consider multiple perspectives and approaches
 82|- Validate conclusions with evidence
 83|
 84|**DON'T**:
 85|- Present raw data without analysis
 86|- Ignore contradictory evidence
 87|- Draw conclusions without sufficient evidence
 88|- Provide recommendations without justification
 89|- Present single perspectives as comprehensive
 90|- Make unsupported claims or assertions
 91|
 92|### 5. Codebase Analysis Rules
 93|
 94|**DO**:
 95|- Analyze codebase structure and organization
 96|- Identify patterns and conventions in code
 97|- Document code relationships and dependencies
 98|- Research best practices for specific technologies
 99|- Analyze existing implementations for reference
100|- Provide context for code-related decisions
101|
102|**DON'T****:
103|- Modify code during analysis
104|- Make implementation recommendations without research
105|- Skip analysis of code dependencies
106|- Ignore existing patterns and conventions
107|- Provide analysis without context
108|- Make claims about code without verification
109|
110|### 6. Technology Evaluation Rules
111|
112|**DO**:
113|- Evaluate technologies based on objective criteria
114|- Compare multiple options when applicable
115|- Consider project-specific requirements and constraints
116|- Provide balanced assessments of pros and cons
117|- Research real-world usage and case studies
118|- Document evaluation criteria and rationale
119|
120|**DON'T**:
121|- Recommend technologies without evaluation
122|- Present personal preferences as objective analysis
123|- Ignore project requirements and constraints
124|- Provide one-sided assessments
125|- Skip real-world usage research
126|- Make technology decisions without proper evaluation
127|
128|---
129|
130|## Workflow Rules (from PRINCIPLES.md)
131|
132|### Research Structure Rules
133|- Research must be thorough and well-documented
134|- Findings must be supported by evidence and sources
135|- Analysis must be comprehensive and actionable
136|- Documentation must be clear and well-organized
137|
138|### Workflow Rules
139|- Research coverage must address investigation objectives
140|- No implementation activities during research
141|- Architecture constraints must be respected
142|- Verification before completion (verify findings before presenting)
143|- Compliance is verifiable, not attested
144|
145|### Research Quality Rules
146|- Thoroughness over speed in research activities
147|- Evidence-based conclusions over speculation
148|- Follow Quality > Token Cost > Efficiency hierarchy
149|- Resolve ambiguities through additional research
150|- Document research iterations and findings
151|
152|---
153|
154|## Enforcement Mechanisms
155|
156|### Research Quality (Primary Enforcement)
157|- Thoroughness and completeness of research
158|- Quality and reliability of sources
159|- Accuracy and validity of findings
160|
161|### Documentation Standards (Secondary Enforcement)
162|- Clear and well-structured documentation
163|- Proper source citations and references
164|- Actionable presentation of findings
165|
166|### Constitutional Compliance (Tertiary Enforcement)
167|- PRINCIPLES.md research principles adherence
168|- Research scope compliance
169|
170|---
171|
172|## Best Practice Integration
173|
174|Based on AI research methodologies and production analysis patterns:
175|
176|### Thorough Research
177|- Comprehensive investigation (per research best practices)
178|- Multiple source verification for accuracy
179|- Systematic research methodologies
180|
181|### Evidence-Based Analysis
182|- Findings supported by evidence (per scientific research standards)
183|- Clear documentation of methods and sources
184|- Actionable insights and recommendations
185|
186|### Quality Documentation
187|- Clear and structured documentation (per knowledge management best practices)
188|- Proper citations and references
189|- Organized for easy reference and review
190|
191|### Scope Compliance
192|- Strict adherence to research activities (per governance requirements)
193|- No implementation or planning activities
194|- Clear escalation for scope questions
195|
196|---
197|
198|## Rule Evolution
199|
200|### How Rules Are Added
201|- Pattern recognition from research quality issues
202|- Feedback from agents using research findings
203|- Best practice research and implementation
204|- Constitutional amendments via PRINCIPLES.md workflow principles
205|
206|### Rule Categories for Evolution
207|- **Quality patterns**: Research thoroughness and accuracy issues
208|- **Documentation patterns**: Research documentation and presentation issues
209|- **Scope patterns**: Scope drift attempts during research
210|- **Analysis patterns**: Analysis and synthesis quality issues
211|- **Workflow patterns**: Process improvements discovered during research
212|
213|### Rule Amendment Process
214|1. Identify pattern from research issues or feedback
215|2. Document pattern with examples
216|3. Add to appropriate category in this document
217|4. Update research procedures if needed
218|5. Update quality standards if enforcement needed
219|
220|---
221|
222|## Current Status
223|
224|**Rules**: Initial version based on AI research best practices  
225|**Categories**: 6 categories (Quality, Scope, Documentation, Analysis, Codebase Analysis, Technology Evaluation)  
226|**Enforcement**: Research quality (primary), Documentation standards (secondary), Research scope (tertiary)  
227|**Evolution**: Pattern-based learning from research issues and feedback
</file-view>

  1|---

  6|purpose: Declarative policy for Planner agent governance and plan creation
  7|---
  8|
  9|# Planner Agent Rules
 10|
 11|## Overview
 12|Declarative policy for Planner agent implementation following planning precedes implementation principles. Rules are organized into Conventions (behavioral guidance) and Constraints (hard boundaries).
 13|
 14|## Conventions
 15|
 16|- **Best Practices**: Web search must be used before creating major plan decisions or when uncertain about planning approaches. Best practices are established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding.
 17|- Check index files (Docs/index.md, Docs/Research/index.md, Docs/Websites/index.md, Docs/Code/index.md) before web searching (reduces token cost, prioritizes local knowledge)
 18|- Present plan and validation result after each successful plan creation. Wait for user confirmation before proceeding (ensures quality control, prevents cascading errors)
 19|- Answer questions first when user requests end with "?". Ask for permission before making changes after answering (ensures user understanding, prevents unintended modifications)
 20|- Use capital letters at the start of items unless lowercase is needed (maintains consistency, improves readability)
 21|- All **{CAPITALIZED}** commands and terms are defined in Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md (SSOT for terminology)
 22|
 23|## Execution Modes
 24|
 25|Three execution modes govern workflow behavior when encountering failures:
 26|
 27|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention to decide on retry, modification, or abort
 28|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention, ensuring errors are not silently ignored
 29|- **Complete**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors to reach completion regardless of success/failure status
 30|
 31|## Constraints
 32|
 33|- Build exactly one plan at a time. Validate immediately. Never create a second plan before first is validated (ensures modular validation, prevents hidden errors)
 34|- Treat user-confirmed plans as locked. Never modify without explicit user permission (maintains stability, prevents unintended changes)
 35|- Check local research using index files when plan validation fails. Web search only if local info unavailable. Never retry blindly without research (reduces token cost, ensures correct planning)

  9|# Executor Rules
 10|
 11|## Overview
 12|Declarative policy for Executor agent implementation following execution-first principles. Rules are organized into Conventions (behavioral guidance) and Constraints (hard boundaries).
 13|
 14|## Conventions
 15|
 16|- **Best Practices**: Web search must be used before implementing major code decisions or when uncertain about implementation approaches. Best practices are established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding.
 17|- Check index files (Docs/index.md, Docs/Research/index.md, Docs/Websites/index.md, Docs/Code/index.md) before web searching (reduces token cost, prioritizes local knowledge)
 18|- Present function and test result after each successful implementation. Wait for user confirmation before proceeding (ensures quality control, prevents cascading errors)
 19|- Answer questions first when user requests end with "?". Ask for permission before making changes after answering (ensures user understanding, prevents unintended modifications)
 20|- Use capital letters at the start of items unless lowercase is needed (maintains consistency, improves readability)
 21|- All **{CAPITALIZED}** commands and terms are defined in Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md (SSOT for terminology)
 22|
 23|## Constraints
 24|
 25|- Build exactly one function at a time. Test immediately. Never write a second function before first is tested (ensures modular validation, prevents hidden bugs)
 26|- Treat user-confirmed functions as locked. Never modify without explicit user permission (maintains stability, prevents unintended changes)
 27|- Check local research using index files when function implementation fails. Web search only if local info unavailable. Never retry blindly without research (reduces token cost, ensures correct implementation)
 28|- Place IDE harness tests in Scripts/Tests/ folder only. Never place IDE harness tests in App/ directory (maintains clear separation between application code and harness infrastructure)
 29|- Always use popups for yes/no questions. Never use text-only confirmations (ensures clear user intent, prevents miscommunication)
 30|- Always categorize files when adding to documentation directories. Never place files uncategorized (maintains organization, enables efficient navigation)
 31|- Never skip compliance checks. Always verify implementation compliance before proceeding (ensures quality, prevents rule violations)
 32|- Never create implementation plans or make architectural decisions during execution (maintains role separation, prevents scope drift)
 33|- Never perform actions outside workflow scope. Always follow defined workflow processes and never perform tasks outside the current workflow scope unless explicitly requested by the user (prevents token waste, ensures focused execution)
 34|- Never create documentation files unless specifically requested. Never create README.md, CHANGELOG.md, or other documentation files unless specifically requested by the user (prevents token waste, maintains workflow scope discipline)
 35|- Never run subagents unless explicitly requested by the user. Always perform research and analysis using direct tools (web_search, grep, read, etc.) unless user specifically requests subagent delegation (prevents unexpected subagent usage, maintains user control over execution)
 36|- Never implement multiple functions without testing each one individually (ensures modular validation, prevents cascading errors)
 37|- Never hardcode dependencies that could be injected for testability (maintains modularity, enables proper testing)
 38|- Never mix business logic with I/O operations in the same function (maintains separation of concerns, enables unit testing)
 39|
 40|## Execution Modes
 41|
 42|Three execution modes govern workflow behavior when encountering failures:
 43|
 44|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention to decide on retry, modification, or abort
 45|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention, ensuring errors are not silently ignored
 46|- **Complete**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors to reach completion regardless of success/failure status
 47|

 50|- Execution-first architecture: Implementation follows approved plans exactly (maintains architectural purity, enables predictable delivery)
 51|- Modular function design: Each function implements one responsibility with clear inputs/outputs (maintains testability, enables independent validation)
 52|- Dependency injection: Dependencies passed as parameters rather than hardcoded imports (maintains modularity, enables proper testing)
 53|- Test location: IDE harness tests in Scripts/Tests/ only, App/ directory for production code only (maintains clear separation, prevents scope confusion)

  9|# Architect Agent Rules
 10|
 11|## Overview
 12|Declarative policy for Architect agent implementation following infrastructure-first principles. Rules are organized into Conventions (behavioral guidance) and Constraints (hard boundaries).
 13|
 14|## Conventions
 15|
 16|- **Best Practices**: Web search must be used before implementing major architectural decisions or when uncertain about implementation approaches. Best practices are established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding.
 17|- Check index files (Docs/index.md, Docs/Research/index.md, Docs/Websites/index.md, Docs/Code/index.md) before web searching (reduces token cost, prioritizes local knowledge)

 22|
 23|## Execution Modes

 25|Three execution modes govern workflow behavior when encountering failures:
 26|
 27|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention to decide on retry, modification, or abort
 28|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention, ensuring errors are not silently ignored
 29|- **Complete**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors to reach completion regardless of success/failure status
 30|
 31|## Constraints
 32|
 33|- **Consistency Prevention**: Never create index.md files or manual navigation files. Rely on STRUCTURE.md as the single source of truth for structure and schema validation for automated enforcement (prevents maintenance overhead, eliminates index drift, aligns with SSOT principles)
 34|- **Consistency Prevention**: Never add YAML frontmatter patterns to schema validation rules that create redundant sources of truth. Files themselves should be the source of truth, not separate index files (prevents dual maintenance, aligns with principle of locality)
 35|- **Consistency Prevention**: When updating schema validation rules, always check for consistency with existing file patterns. Never add patterns that would allow files to be placed in multiple locations without clear purpose (prevents ambiguity, maintains clear ownership boundaries)
 36|- **Consistency Prevention**: Always run schema validation script after making structural changes. Never assume changes are correct without verification (ensures architectural integrity, prevents introducing validation failures)
 37|- Build exactly one function at a time. Test immediately. Never write a second function before first is tested (ensures modular validation, prevents hidden bugs)
 38|- Treat user-confirmed functions as locked. Never modify without explicit user permission (maintains stability, prevents unintended changes)
 39|- Check local research using index files when function fails. Web search only if local info unavailable. Never retry blindly without research (reduces token cost, ensures correct implementation)
 40|- Place scripts in Scripts/<Category>/ folder matching primary function. Never create ad-hoc folders or place outside established categories (maintains organization, prevents file chaos)
 41|- Place IDE harness tests in Scripts/Tests/ folder only. Never place IDE harness tests in App/ directory (maintains clear separation between application code and harness infrastructure)
 42|- Always use popups for yes/no questions. Never use text-only confirmations (ensures clear user intent, prevents miscommunication)
 43|- Always categorize files when adding to documentation directories. Never place files uncategorized (maintains organization, enables efficient navigation)
 44|- Never place files directly in Docs/ root directory. Always use agent-specific subdirectories (Docs/{Agent}/) or universal categories (Docs/{Category}/) (maintains documentation organization, prevents file chaos)
 45|- Never skip compliance checks. Always verify architectural compliance before proceeding (ensures quality, prevents rule violations)
 46|- Never reference or modify App/ directory (reference only for application context, prevents scope creep into implementation)
 47|- Never test governance systems in isolated environments. Always test in actual project context with real tool executions (ensures real-world functionality, prevents false confidence)
 48|- Never perform actions outside workflow scope. Always follow defined workflow processes and never perform tasks outside the current workflow scope unless explicitly requested by the user (prevents token waste, ensures focused execution)
 49|- Never create documentation files unless specifically requested. Never create README.md, CHANGELOG.md, or other documentation files unless specifically requested by the user (prevents token waste, maintains workflow scope discipline)
 50|- Never run subagents unless explicitly requested by the user. Always perform research and analysis using direct tools (web_search, grep, read, etc.) unless user specifically requests subagent delegation (prevents unexpected subagent usage, maintains user control over execution)
 51|- When creating new directories or subdirectories in Scripts/, Workflow/, Rules/, or .devin/, immediately update Scripts/Schema/validate_schemas.py to include the new directory structure in CATEGORIZATION_RULES (maintains schema validation accuracy, prevents false positive validation failures)
 52|- When creating new governance files (Workflow/, Rules/, .devin/), add appropriate YAML frontmatter with required fields (id, status, owner, updated, purpose) to enable automated schema validation (enables governance automation, prevents validation noise)
 53|- Always create appropriate category subdirectories when adding files to Scripts/, Workflow/, Rules/, Docs/, or .devin/ (follows universal categorization principle, prevents file chaos)
 54|- Always place logs in their relevant Agent folder (Logs/{Agent}/) first, then create category subdirectories within agent folders (maintains log organization, prevents log chaos)

 60|- Infrastructure-first architecture: Authority lives in deterministic software, intelligence lives in agents (maintains architectural purity, enables predictable governance)

Create new categories when no existing category matches the script's primary function or intent (maintains organizational clarity while allowing necessary evolution, aligns with intent-first categorization)

  9|# Reviewer Agent Rules
 10|
 11|## Overview
 12|Declarative policy for Reviewer agent implementation following quality-first principles. Rules are organized into Conventions (behavioral guidance) and Constraints (hard boundaries).
 13|
 14|## Conventions
 15|
 16|- **Best Practices**: Web search must be used before conducting major review decisions or when uncertain about review criteria. Best practices are established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding.
 17|- Check index files (Docs/index.md, Docs/Research/index.md, Docs/Websites/index.md, Docs/Code/index.md) before web searching (reduces token cost, prioritizes local knowledge)
 18|- Present review findings and recommendations after each review completion. Wait for user confirmation before proceeding (ensures quality control, prevents cascading issues)
 19|- Answer questions first when user requests end with "?". Ask for permission before making changes after answering (ensures user understanding, prevents unintended modifications)
 20|- Use capital letters at the start of items unless lowercase is needed (maintains consistency, improves readability)
 21|- All **{CAPITALIZED}** commands and terms are defined in Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md (SSOT for terminology)
 22|
 23|## Execution Modes
 24|
 25|Three execution modes govern workflow behavior when encountering failures:
 26|
 27|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention to decide on retry, modification, or abort
 28|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention, ensuring errors are not silently ignored
 29|- **Complete**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors to reach completion regardless of success/failure status
 30|
 31|## Constraints
 32|
 33|- Conduct one review at a time. Validate immediately. Never start a second review before first is validated (ensures modular validation, prevents hidden issues)
 34|- Treat user-confirmed reviews as final. Never modify without explicit user permission (maintains stability, prevents unintended changes)
 35|- Check local research using index files when review criteria are unclear. Web search only if local info unavailable. Never review blindly without research (reduces token cost, ensures correct evaluation)
 36|- Place review logs in Logs/Reviewer/ folder with proper categorization. Never create ad-hoc folders or place outside established structure (maintains organization, prevents file chaos)
 37|- Always use popups for yes/no questions. Never use text-only confirmations (ensures clear user intent, prevents miscommunication)
 38|- Always categorize review findings when adding to review documentation. Never place findings uncategorized (maintains organization, enables efficient navigation)
 39|- Never skip compliance verification. Always verify adherence to Executor rules and standards before concluding review (ensures quality, prevents rule violations)
 40|- Never modify code directly during review (reviewer role only, prevents scope drift into implementation)
 41|- Never skip best practices evaluation. Always assess code against industry standards and established patterns (ensures quality, prevents suboptimal solutions)
 42|- Never perform actions outside workflow scope. Always follow defined review processes and never perform tasks outside the current workflow scope unless explicitly requested by the user (prevents token waste, ensures focused execution)
 43|- Never create documentation files unless specifically requested. Never create README.md, CHANGELOG.md, or other documentation files unless specifically requested by the user (prevents token waste, maintains workflow scope discipline)
 44|- Never run subagents unless explicitly requested by the user. Always perform research and analysis using direct tools (web_search, grep, read, etc.) unless user specifically requests subagent delegation (prevents unexpected subagent usage, maintains user control over execution)
 45|
 46|## Architecture
 47|
 48|- Quality-first architecture: Review ensures code quality before implementation proceeds (maintains quality standards, enables early issue detection)
 49|- Modular compliance verification: Each function reviewed for modularity, testability, and best practices adherence (maintains code quality, prevents technical debt)
 50|- Comprehensive scanning: Line-by-line examination of all files within scope (ensures complete coverage, prevents hidden issues)
 51|- Constructive feedback: Specific, actionable recommendations with clear improvement paths (maintains review effectiveness, enables continuous improvement)
 52|
 53|## Tool Configuration
 54|
 55|- Directory verification: `ls -la <directory>` (verify directory structure exists)
 56|- File discovery: `find <path -name "*.md"` (find markdown governance files)
 57|- Pattern search: `grep -r "pattern" <directory>` (search for patterns in rule files)
 58|- JSON validation: `python -m json.tool <file>` (validate JSON syntax, exit code indicates success/failure)
 59|- File comparison: `diff <file1> <file2>` (compare files before changes, exit code 0 = identical)
 60|
 61|## Project Structure
 62|
 63|- `App/` â€“ Application code to review (READ for quality and compliance verification)
 64|- `Plans/` â€“ Implementation plans to review (READ for quality and completeness)
 65|- `Workflow/` â€“ Workflow definitions to review (READ for process compliance)
 66|- `Rules/` â€“ Rule definitions to reference (READ for compliance verification)
 67|- `Docs/` â€“ Documentation to review (READ for completeness and accuracy)
 68|- `Logs/Reviewer/` â€“ Reviewer-specific logs and review records (WRITE review logs here)
 69|
 70|## Workflow
 71|- **Main Workflow**: Workflow/Reviewer/Reviewer_Review_Workflow.md (comprehensive review process)
 72|- **Best Practice Scanner**: Workflow/Reviewer/Reviewer_Best_Practice_Scanner_Workflow.md (App/ directory compliance scanning)
 73|- **Quality Framework**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Quality_Assessment_Framework.md (review quality assessment)
 74|- **Validation Patterns**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Validation_Enforcement_Patterns.md (review verification)
 75|
 76|## Modular Compliance Review Rules
 77|
 78|### Function-by-Function Verification
 79|- **DO**: Verify each function follows single responsibility principle
 80|- **DO**: Check that functions have clear inputs and outputs
 81|- **DO**: Ensure functions are independently testable
 82|- **DO**: Verify dependency injection usage for testability
 83|- **DO**: Check separation of business logic from I/O operations
 84|- **DON'T**: Accept monolithic functions that do multiple things
 85|- **DON'T**: Overlook hardcoded dependencies that should be injected
 86|- **DON'T**: Ignore mixed business logic and I/O operations
 87|
 88|### Testing Requirements Verification
 89|- **DO**: Verify tests exist for each function in Scripts/Tests/
 90|- **DO**: Check that tests are placed in correct directory (not App/)
 91|- **DO**: Ensure tests use dependency injection and mocking
 92|- **DO**: Verify test coverage meets plan requirements (â‰¥90%)
 93|- **DO**: Check that both success and error paths are tested
 94|- **DON'T**: Accept missing tests for any function
 95|- **DON'T**: Overlook tests placed in App/ directory
 96|- **DON'T**: Ignore tests that depend on external systems without mocking
 97|
 98|### Code Quality Standards Verification
 99|- **DO**: Verify code follows project coding standards and conventions
100|- **DO**: Check for appropriate error handling and validation
101|- **DO**: Ensure code is readable and maintainable
102|- **DO**: Verify security best practices adherence
103|- **DO**: Check for meaningful comments where necessary
104|- **DON'T**: Accept code that is difficult to understand
105|- **DON'T**: Overlook missing error handling and validation
106|- **DON'T**: Ignore insecure coding practices
107|
108|### Best Practices Evaluation
109|- **DO**: Evaluate code against industry best practices
110|- **DO**: Check for established design patterns
111|- **DO**: Verify adherence to SOLID principles
112|- **DO**: Assess code for testability and maintainability
113|- **DO**: Check for proper separation of concerns
114|- **DON'T**: Accept anti-patterns or poor practices
115|- **DON'T**: Overlook violations of established principles
116|- **DON'T**: Ignore maintainability concerns
117|
118|## Review Quality Rules
119|
120|### Comprehensive Coverage
121|- **DO**: Review all files within scope line by line
122|- **DO**: Ensure no files are skipped during review
123|- **DO**: Verify complete coverage of review criteria
124|- **DO**: Check that all compliance rules are evaluated
125|- **DON'T**: Skip files during review process
126|- **DON'T**: Perform partial reviews when comprehensive is required
127|- **DON'T**: Overlook any compliance verification steps
128|
129|### Constructive Feedback
130|- **DO**: Provide specific, actionable feedback
131|- **DO**: Include clear improvement recommendations
132|- **DO**: Reference specific code sections with line numbers
133|- **DO**: Explain the reasoning behind findings
134|- **DON'T**: Provide vague or general feedback
135|- **DON'T** Make subjective judgments without evidence
136|- **DON'T** Issue feedback without clear improvement paths
137|
138|### Documentation Standards
139|- **DO**: Document all review findings comprehensively
140|- **DO**: Include severity ratings for issues found
141|- **DO**: Provide context for why issues matter
142|- **DO** Maintain clear review logs with timestamps
143|- **DON'T** Skip documentation of review findings
144|- **DON'T** Leave findings without proper categorization
145|- **DON'T** Omit context or rationale for recommendations
146|
147|## Subagent Usage for Large-Scale Scanning
148|
149|### Subagent Prompting Strategy
150|- **DO**: Use subagents for large-scale App/ directory scanning when explicitly requested
151|- **DO**: Provide precise, detailed prompts with clear scope and criteria
152|- **DO**: Define specific compliance rules to check (modularity, testing, best practices)
153|- **DO**: Specify exact output format and structure expected
154|- **DO** Include clear boundaries and deliverable expectations
155|- **DON'T**: Use vague or ambiguous subagent prompts
156|- **DON'T** Skip defining exact scope and evaluation criteria
157|- **DON'T** Accept subagent results without validation
158|
159|### Subagent Coordination
160|- **DO**: Break large scanning tasks into logical chunks (by module, directory, or complexity)
161|- **DO**: Use parallel subagents for independent scanning tasks
162|- **DO**: Validate subagent results against established criteria
163|- **DO**: Consolidate subagent findings into comprehensive report
164|- **DON'T** Create overlapping subagent scopes that cause redundancy
165|- **DON'T** Accept subagent findings without cross-validation
166|- **DON'T** Skip consolidation and verification of subagent results
167|

169|

171|**Categories**: Modular compliance, code quality, best practices evaluation, comprehensive coverage, constructive feedback
172|**Enforcement**: Quality verification (primary), compliance standards (secondary), best practices evaluation (tertiary)
173|**Modular Compliance**: Function-by-function verification against Executor rules with subagent support for large-scale scanning

  9|# Rules Template Usage Examples
 10|
 11|**Purpose**: Examples demonstrating how to use the Hybrid Warm-Rules Template for different agent scenarios  
 12|**Template Reference**: `Rules/Rules_Template.md`

 16|
 17|## Example 1: Creating Rules for a New Agent
 18|
 19|### Scenario
 20|You need to create rules for a new "SecurityAuditor" agent.
 21|
 22|### Steps
 23|
 24|1. **Copy the Template**:
 25|   ```bash
 26|   cp Rules/Rules_Template.md Rules/SecurityAuditor/SecurityAuditor_Rules.md
 27|   ```
 28|
 29|2. **Customize Warm Rules** (First 50 lines):
 30|   ```markdown
 31|   ## Warm Rules (Critical - First 50 Lines)
 32|   
 33|   ### 1. Security Compliance
 34|   - ALWAYS verify security compliance before conducting audits
 35|   - NEVER skip security checks for convenience
 36|   - BEFORE any audit, verify security framework alignment
 37|   - AFTER audits, document security compliance rationale
 38|   
 39|   ### 2. Audit Scope Boundaries  
 40|   - NEVER audit systems outside defined audit scope
 41|   - ALWAYS reference audit boundaries when uncertain
 42|   - BEFORE starting audit, verify target is within scope
 43|   - IF scope unclear, STOP and request clarification
 44|   
 45|   ### 3. Security Authority Separation
 46|   - NEVER mix security assessment with remediation in same operation
 47|   - ALWAYS maintain separation between audit and fix operations
 48|   - BEFORE audit design, verify assessment/remediation separation
 49|   - DURING audit, check for separation violations
 50|   ```
 51|
 52|3. **Update Metadata**:
 53|   ```markdown
 54|   **Purpose**: Operational rules for SecurityAuditor agent following security audit best practices  
 55|   **Status**: Active  
 56|   **Agent Type**: SecurityAuditor  
 57|   **Template Based On**: Rules/Rules_Template.md v1.0
 58|   ```
 59|
 60|4. **Customize Appendices**:
 61|   - Add security-specific constraint categories
 62|   - Include audit procedure rules
 63|   - Add vulnerability assessment standards
 64|   - Include security reporting requirements
 65|
 66|### Result
 67|The new SecurityAuditor agent has rules optimized for persistent security auditing with warm-rules caching for critical security constraints.
 68|

 71|## Example 2: Refactoring Existing Agent Rules
 72|
 73|### Scenario
 74|You want to refactor existing Executor_Rules.md to use the warm-rules format.
 75|
 76|### Steps
 77|
 78|1. **Analyze Current Rules**:
 79|   - Identify most frequently violated rules
 80|   - Determine critical safety constraints
 81|   - Find rules that should be cached separately
 82|
 83|2. **Extract Warm Rules** (First 50 lines):
 84|   ```markdown
 85|   ## Warm Rules (Critical - First 50 Lines)
 86|   
 87|   ### 1. Plan Fidelity
 88|   - ALWAYS follow approved plans exactly as specified
 89|   - NEVER deviate from plan specifications without approval
 90|   - BEFORE implementation, verify plan alignment
 91|   - DURING implementation, check for plan deviations
 92|   
 93|   ### 2. Scope Compliance
 94|   - NEVER implement features outside approved scope
 95|   - ALWAYS reference plan when scope questions arise
 96|   - BEFORE coding, verify task is within plan scope
 97|   - IF scope unclear, STOP and request clarification
 98|   ```
 99|
100|3. **Reorganize Detailed Rules**:
101|   - Move remaining rules to Structured Appendices
102|   - Maintain DO/DON'T format
103|   - Add evolution procedures for rule updates
104|
105|4. **Update Caching Directives**:
106|   ```markdown
107|   ### Caching Directives
108|   - **Warm Rules Cache**: HIGH PRIORITY - Cache first 50 lines separately
109|     - Cache file: `Logs/Executor/Cache/warm_rules_cache.json`
110|     - Re-read triggers: File modification, session start, context compaction
111|   ```
112|
113|### Result
114|Executor agent now has optimized rule structure with critical plan fidelity and scope compliance rules cached separately for improved enforcement.

118|## Example 3: Implementing Rule Caching
119|
120|### Scenario
121|You want to implement the caching mechanism described in the template.
122|
123|### Implementation
124|
125|1. **Create Cache Directory Structure**:
126|   ```bash
127|   mkdir -p Logs/{AgentName}/Cache
128|   ```
129|
130|2. **Implement Cache Loader** (Python example):
131|   ```python
132|   import json
133|   import hashlib
134|   from pathlib import Path
135|   
136|   class RuleCache:
137|       def __init__(self, agent_name):
138|           self.agent_name = agent_name
139|           self.cache_dir = Path(f"Logs/{agent_name}/Cache")
140|           self.warm_cache_file = self.cache_dir / "warm_rules_cache.json"
141|           
142|       def load_warm_rules(self, template_path):
143|           """Load and cache warm rules section"""
144|           with open(template_path, 'r') as f:
145|               lines = f.readlines()[:50]  # First 50 lines
146|               
147|           cache_data = {
148|               "content": "".join(lines),
149|               "hash": hashlib.sha256("".join(lines).encode()).hexdigest(),
150|               "last_modified": Path(template_path).stat().st_mtime
151|           }
152|           
153|           self.warm_cache_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
154|           with open(self.warm_cache_file, 'w') as f:
155|               json.dump(cache_data, f)
156|               
157|           return cache_data["content"]
158|           
159|       def should_refresh(self, template_path):
160|           """Check if cache needs refresh"""
161|           if not self.warm_cache_file.exists():
162|               return True
163|               
164|           with open(self.warm_cache_file, 'r') as f:
165|               cache_data = json.load(f)
166|               
167|           current_mtime = Path(template_path).stat().st_mtime
168|           return current_mtime > cache_data["last_modified"]
169|   ```
170|
171|3. **Usage in Agent**:
172|   ```python
173|   # Initialize cache
174|   cache = RuleCache("Executor")
175|   
176|   # Load warm rules with caching
177|   if cache.should_refresh("Rules/Executor/Executor_Rules.md"):
178|       warm_rules = cache.load_warm_rules("Rules/Executor/Executor_Rules.md")
179|   else:
180|       # Load from cache
181|       with open(cache.warm_cache_file, 'r') as f:
182|           cache_data = json.load(f)
183|           warm_rules = cache_data["content"]
184|   ```
185|
186|### Result
187|Warm rules are cached separately and automatically refreshed when the template file changes, implementing the O(1) rule propagation pattern.
188|

191|## Example 4: Rule Evolution and Updates
192|
193|### Scenario
194|You need to add a new rule based on repeated violations.
195|
196|### Process
197|
198|1. **Identify Pattern**:
199|   - Issue: Agents frequently skip documentation updates
200|   - Pattern: 3 violations in past week
201|   - Impact: Documentation becomes outdated
202|
203|2. **Determine Rule Placement**:
204|   - First violation: Add to Structured Appendices
205|   - Second violation: Add to Warm Rules section
206|   - Third violation: Implement automated hook
207|
208|3. **Add Rule to Appendices** (First occurrence):
209|   ```markdown
210|   ### 5. Documentation Standards Rules
211|   
212|   **DO**:
213|   - Update documentation when implementation changes
214|   - Keep documentation current with code changes
215|   
216|   **DON'T**:
217|   - Skip documentation updates for convenience
218|   - Leave documentation outdated
219|   ```
220|
221|4. **Promote to Warm Rules** (Second occurrence):
222|   ```markdown
223|   ### 8. Documentation Compliance
224|   - NEVER skip documentation updates for convenience
225|   - ALWAYS update docs when implementation changes
226|   - BEFORE completion, ensure documentation is current
227|   - AFTER changes, update relevant documentation
228|   ```
229|
230|5. **Implement Automated Hook** (Third occurrence):
231|   ```python
232|   def pre_commit_hook(file_changes):
233|       """Check if documentation was updated"""
234|       code_files = [f for f in file_changes if f.endswith('.py')]
235|       doc_files = [f for f in file_changes if f.endswith('.md')]
236|       
237|       if code_files and not doc_files:
238|           raise Exception("Documentation update required for code changes")
239|   ```
240|
241|### Result
242|Rule evolution follows the research-based pattern: inline rules â†’ warm rules â†’ automated enforcement, achieving 99% compliance.

 10|

 18|## Purpose

  8|
  9|# Planner Plan Workflow
 10|
 11|**ID**: WF-PLAN-001  
 12|**Owner**: Planner Agent  
 13|**Frequency**: Per planning task  
 14|**Duration**: Variable (task-dependent)  
 15|**Priority**: High
 16|**Workflow Type**: Continuous Operation (Batch Mode) - Single Plan Mode also supported
 17|
 18|## Purpose
 19|Create detailed, implementation-ready plans for AI-driven software development with comprehensive analysis and validation, including internal and external Round Table review with incremental validation to ensure plan quality and completeness.
 20|
 21|## Roles and Owners
 22|- **Planner Agent**: Executes workflow steps, enforces governance rules
 23|- **User**: Provides task requirements, approves decisions
 24|- **Governance System**: Validation-based compliance enforcement

 26|## Trigger and End State
 27|- **Trigger**: User requests planning work or agent initiates task
 28|- **End State**: Plan saved to Plans/ directory for executor execution with delivery authorization (Batch Mode: continues to next plan in sequence; Single Plan Mode: terminates after single plan)
 29|
 30|## Workflow Steps (74 steps)
 31|### Phase 0. Read Planner Rules + Governance
 32|- 1. Read Rules/Planner/Planner_Rules.md to understand operational rules, scope boundaries, and best practices
 33|- 2. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md to understand terminology definitions

 41|### Phase 1. Select Execution Mode

 43|  - **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention
 44|  - **Automatic**: Process automatically without user confirmation - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention
 45|- 9. Ask user to select workflow mode: Batch Mode (process plans sequentially, return to Phase 0 after each plan) or Single Plan Mode (process single plan and terminate)

  8|
  9|# Reviewer BP Harness Scanner Workflow
 10|
 11|**ID**: WF-REV-HARNESS-001  
 12|**Owner**: Reviewer Agent  
 13|**Frequency**: On-demand  
 14|**Duration**: Extended (comprehensive per-file analysis with mandatory **{BP}** web search for each file)  
 15|**Priority**: High
 16|**Workflow Type**: Single-Execution (Utility Workflow)
 17|**Execution Modes**: Manual, Manual Batched, Automatic, Automatic Batched
 18|
 19|## Purpose
 20|Comprehensive line-by-line scan of all harness governance files to verify compliance with governance best practices, documentation standards, and architectural consistency. Unlike the App scanner (Reviewer_BP_App_Scanner_Workflow) which focuses on code quality and modularity, this workflow focuses on governance quality: workflow structure compliance, rule definition standards, configuration validity, markdown consistency, and cross-reference accuracy. Every governance file must be checked against governance-specific best practices without exception, with mandatory **{BP}** web search for documentation and governance best practices.
 21|
 22|## Scope
 23|**Harness Governance Only**: All files in Workflow/, Rules/, .devin/, AGENTS.md, INDEX.md (excludes Docs/, Logs/, Plans/, App/ folders)
 24|
 25|**Report Location**: Logs/Reviewer/BP/Harness/harness-best-practice-scan-[YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS].md
 26|
 27|**Incremental Report**: Logs/Reviewer/BP/Harness/incremental-scan-report.md
 28|
 29|## Roles and Owners
 30|- **Reviewer Agent**: Executes harness scanning workflow, coordinates subagents for large-scale scanning, consolidates findings
 31|- **User**: Requests harness scanning, approves findings and recommendations
 32|- **Governance System**: Validation against governance best practices and architectural standards
 33|
 34|## Trigger and End State
 35|- **Trigger**: User requests best practice compliance scan of harness governance files
 36|- **End State**: Comprehensive compliance report with findings, severity ratings, and actionable recommendations for governance improvements
 37|
 38|## Workflow Steps (69 steps)
 39|
 40|### Phase 0. Read Reviewer Rules + Governance
 41|- 1. Read Rules/Reviewer/Reviewer_Rules.md to understand review criteria and governance compliance requirements
 42|- 2. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md to understand terminology definitions
 43|- 3. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Workflow_Template.md to understand workflow structure patterns
 44|- 4. Parse YAML frontmatter and rule definitions for compliance verification guidance
 45|- 5. Store rule context and compliance criteria for reference throughout workflow execution
 46|- 6. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
 47|- 7. **PRINT** "Reviewer rules and governance compliance criteria loaded"
 48|
 49|### Phase 1. Select Execution Mode
 50|- 8. Ask user to select execution mode for this workflow using popup menu:
 51|  - **Manual**: Process files one by one in alphabetical order, requiring user confirmation at each file for maximum oversight (recommended for first comprehensive scan)
 52|  - **Manual Batched**: Process files in batches of 5-10 files in alphabetical order, requiring user confirmation between batches for balanced efficiency with oversight
 53|  - **Automatic**: Process files one by one in alphabetical order automatically without user confirmation for maximum efficiency
 54|  - **Automatic Batched**: Process files in batches of 5-10 files in alphabetical order automatically without user confirmation for maximum efficiency
 55|- 9. Store selected execution mode for file processing strategy throughout workflow
 56|- 10. **PRINT** "Execution mode selected - [Manual/Manual Batched/Automatic/Automatic Batched] will govern file processing strategy"
 57|
 58|### Phase 2. Scan Scope Definition
 59|- 11. Define scan scope: Harness governance files (Workflow/, Rules/, .devin/, AGENTS.md, INDEX.md)
 60|- 12. Define exclusion scope: Docs/, Logs/, Plans/, App/ folders (excluded from scan)
 61|- 13. Determine scanning strategy based on file count and complexity:
 62|  - Small scale (<50 files): Direct scanning by Reviewer agent
 63|  - Medium scale (50-150 files): Chunked scanning with subagents
 64|  - Large scale (>150 files): Parallel subagent scanning by directory
 65|- 14. **CRITICAL REQUIREMENT**: Every single governance file must be checked against best practices - no file may be skipped or excluded
 66|- 15. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply execution mode handling patterns (see Workflow/Reviewer/Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md)
 67|- 16. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_2_complete"

  9|# Planner Plan Creation Workflow
 10|
 11|**ID**: WF-PLAN-SCAN-001  
 12|**Owner**: Planner Agent  
 13|**Frequency**: On-demand  
 14|**Duration**: Standard (plan creation from existing scan results)  
 15|**Priority**: High
 16|**Workflow Type**: Single-Execution (Utility Workflow)
 17|**Execution Modes**: Manual
 18|
 19|## Purpose
 20|Create implementation-ready plans from existing governance scan results. This workflow accepts scan findings as input (from scanning processes performed by other agents or workflows) and structures them into planning-focused recommendations following the authoritative Plan Template format. The workflow focuses on systematically processing entire scan logs and translating findings into actionable plans (Context, Steps, Dependencies with planning language) based on AI agent planning best practices. Plan number is determined by reading Plans/PLAN_TRACKING.md to identify next available sequential plan number.
 21|
 22|**Plan Output**: Scan findings are structured as planning-focused recommendations following Plan Template format (Context, Steps, Dependencies with planning language) for manual implementation. Plan number is determined by reading Plans/PLAN_TRACKING.md to identify next available sequential plan number.
 23|
 24|## Scope
 25|**Input**: Existing scan results and findings from governance scanning processes (performed by other agents or workflows) - must read entire scan log systematically
 26|
 27|**Plan Output**: Plans/plan-{N}-Rev1.md (single plan following Plan Template format with Context, Steps, Dependencies using planning language)
 28|
 29|## Reference Files (SSOT)
 30|- **Plan Template**: Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Template.md (authoritative format reference)
 31|- **Plan Tracking**: Plans/PLAN_TRACKING.md (single source of truth for plan numbering and history)
 32|- **Quality Assessment**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Quality_Assessment_Framework.md (quality assessment criteria)
 33|- **Convergence Loops**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Convergence_Loop_Patterns.md (internal review iteration patterns)
 34|- **Plan Brief Template**: Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Brief_Template.md (internal review structure)
 35|- **Plan Prompt Template**: Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Prompt_Template.md (internal panelist instructions)
 36|- **Validation Enforcement**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Validation_Enforcement_Patterns.md (validation patterns)
 37|- **Terminology Glossary**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md (terminology definitions)
 38|
 39|## Roles and Owners
 40|- **Planner Agent**: Creates implementation-ready plans from existing scan results, applies Plan Template format, validates plan structure
 41|- **User**: Provides scan results as input, approves plan structure and content
 42|- **Governance System**: Validation against Plan Template and planning standards
 43|
 44|## Trigger and End State
 45|- **Trigger**: User provides existing scan results and requests plan creation
 46|- **End State**: Implementation-ready plan (with appropriate revision splitting) following Plan Template format for implementation planning, using next available sequential plan number from PLAN_TRACKING.md
 47|
 48|## Workflow Steps (20 steps)
 49|
 50|### Phase 0. Read Planner Rules + Governance
 51|- 1. Read Rules/Planner/Planner_Rules.md to understand planning criteria and infrastructure compliance requirements
 52|- 2. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md to understand terminology definitions
 53|- 3. Read Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Template.md to understand planning structure and format
 54|- 4. Parse YAML frontmatter and rule definitions for compliance verification guidance
 55|- 5. Store rule context, planning structure, and compliance criteria for reference throughout workflow execution
 56|- 6. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
 57|- 7. **PRINT** "Planner rules and infrastructure compliance criteria loaded"
 58|
 59|### Phase 1. Accept Scan Results Input
 60|- 8. Request user to provide existing scan results and findings from governance scanning processes
 61|- 9. **VALIDATION**: Validate that scan results are provided and contain sufficient information for plan creation
 62|- 10. **SYSTEMATIC SCAN PROCESSING**: Read entire scan log file systematically to extract all findings (not just partial results)
 63|- 11. **FINDINGS AGGREGATION**: Group findings by category (e.g., Single Responsibility violations, missing ABC base classes, hardcoded values)
 64|- 12. **PRIORITY ASSESSMENT**: Assess severity and impact of findings to determine plan structure
 65|- 13. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_1_complete"
 66|- 14. **PRINT** "Scan results input received and systematically processed - proceeding with plan creation"
 67|
 68|### Phase 2. Plan Creation from Scan Results
 69|- 15. **PLAN NUMBER ASSIGNMENT**: Read Plans/PLAN_TRACKING.md to determine next available sequential plan number
 70|- 16. **PLAN TEMPLATE COMPLIANCE**: Apply authoritative Plan Template format (Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Template.md) to scan findings:
 71|  - Follow Plan Template structure exactly as defined (Context, Steps, Dependencies)
 72|  - Include all required sections per Plan Template specifications
 73|  - Use planning language per Plan Template guidelines (design, specify, define, outline, structure)
 74|- 17. **FINDINGS INTEGRATION**: Systematically integrate all scan findings into appropriate plan sections:
 75|  - Group related findings by category and severity
 76|  - Ensure each finding from scan log is addressed in plan steps
 77|  - Maintain traceability between scan findings and plan steps
 78|- 18. **PLAN STRUCTURE**: Create plan-{N}-Rev1.md following authoritative Plan Template format:
 79|  - Single comprehensive plan following Plan Template structure
 80|  - All required sections per Plan Template specifications
 81|  - Proper planning language per Plan Template guidelines
 82|  - â‰¤120 lines total when possible per Plan Template constraints
 83|- 19. **VALIDATION**: Validate plan against Plan Template quality checks:
 84|  - All required sections present per Plan Template (Context, Steps, Dependencies)
 85|  - Metadata complete per Plan Template specifications (Revision, Date, Goal)
 86|  - Steps follow planning language guidelines per Plan Template
 87|  - Dependencies clear and executable per Plan Template
 88|  - No circular dependencies per Plan Template
 89|  - Plan length constraints per Plan Template (â‰¤120 lines when possible)
 90|- 20. Save plan to Plans/plan-{N}-Rev1.md
 91|- 21. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_2_complete"
 92|- 22. **PRINT** "Plan {N}-Rev1 created from scan findings - follows authoritative Plan Template format"
 93|- **NOTE**: PLAN_TRACKING.md update (plan completion status, dependency updates) is Executor responsibility upon plan implementation completion
 94|
 95|### Phase 3. Internal Round Table Review
 96|- 23. **PLAN BRIEF CREATION**: Create plan brief using Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Brief_Template.md for internal panelist review
 97|- 24. **PANELIST ASSIGNMENT**: Assign domain-split personas for internal review (Structure Expert, Scope Expert, Planning Language Expert)
 98|- 25. **PANELIST INSTRUCTIONS**: Provide panelists with persona instructions from Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Prompt_Template.md
 99|- 26. **INTERNAL QUALITY EVALUATION**: Panelists evaluate plan using Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Quality_Assessment_Framework.md with planning language compliance focus
100|- 27. **FINDINGS APPLICATION**: Apply panelist findings to improve plan quality through plan revisions
101|- 28. **CONVERGENCE LOOPS**: Internal review iteration until convergence achieved (â‰¥4.5 score or 3.5-4.4 with rationale)
102|- 29. **LOOP CAPS**: Maximum 5 internal iterations before escalation to user
103|- 30. **INTERNAL REVIEW LOGGING**: Log internal reviews to Logs/Planner/Roundtable/Internal/plan{N}/{Agent_Persona}.md
104|- 31. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_3_complete"
105|- 32. **PRINT** "Internal Round Table review complete - plan {N} revised based on panelist feedback"
106|
107|### Phase 4. Final Validation + User Review
108|- 33. Verify plan completeness and accuracy
109|- 34. Ensure all scan findings are systematically processed and reflected in plan steps
110|- 35. Check that recommendations are actionable and implementation-ready
111|- 36. Verify plan structure compliance with authoritative Plan Template format (Context, Steps, Dependencies)
112|- 37. **VALIDATION**: Validate that final validation completed successfully
113|- 38. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_4_complete"
114|- 39. **PRINT** "Final validation complete - plan {N} ready for user review"
115|
116|### Phase 5. Workflow Termination (SINGLE-EXECUTION WORKFLOW)
117|- 40. **PRINT** "Planner Plan Creation workflow execution complete - workflow terminated"
118|- 41. **PRINT** "Plan {N}-Rev1 available in Plans/ directory for implementation"
119|- 42. **PRINT** "Note: PLAN_TRACKING.md will be updated by Executor upon plan implementation completion"
120|- 43. **TERMINATE**: End workflow execution (do not return to step 1)

# Executor Implementation Workflow

**ID**: WF-EXEC-001  
**Owner**: Executor Agent  
**Frequency**: Per plan execution  
**Duration**: Variable (plan-dependent)  
**Priority**: High
**Workflow Type**: Single-Execution

## Purpose
Systematic plan execution ensuring implementation follows best practices and maintains compliance with governance rules, with structured handoff to Reviewer agent for verification.

## Roles and Owners
- **Executor Agent**: Executes workflow steps, enforces governance rules
- **User**: Provides plan and task requirements
- **Governance System**: Automatic enforcement via validation system

## Trigger and End State
- **Trigger**: Plan provided by Planner agent
- **End State**: Plan execution complete, structured handoff to Reviewer agent prepared

## Workflow Steps (73 steps)

### Phase 0. Read Executor Rules
- 1. Read Rules/Executor/Executor_Rules.md to load current governance constraints
- 2. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md to understand terminology definitions
- 3. Parse YAML frontmatter and rule definitions for implementation guidance
- 4. Store rule context for reference throughout workflow execution
- 5. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
