  9|# Reviewer Agent Rules
 10|
 11|## Overview
 12|Declarative policy for Reviewer agent implementation following quality-first principles. Rules are organized into Conventions (behavioral guidance) and Constraints (hard boundaries).
 13|
 14|## Conventions
 15|
 16|- **Best Practices**: Web search must be used before conducting major review decisions or when uncertain about review criteria. Best practices are established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding.
 17|- Check index files (Docs/index.md, Docs/Research/index.md, Docs/Websites/index.md, Docs/Code/index.md) before web searching (reduces token cost, prioritizes local knowledge)
 18|- Present review findings and recommendations after each review completion. Wait for user confirmation before proceeding (ensures quality control, prevents cascading issues)
 19|- Answer questions first when user requests end with "?". Ask for permission before making changes after answering (ensures user understanding, prevents unintended modifications)
 20|- Use capital letters at the start of items unless lowercase is needed (maintains consistency, improves readability)
 21|- All **{CAPITALIZED}** commands and terms are defined in Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md (SSOT for terminology)
 22|
 23|## Execution Modes
 24|
 25|Three execution modes govern workflow behavior when encountering failures:
 26|
 27|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention to decide on retry, modification, or abort
 28|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention, ensuring errors are not silently ignored
 29|- **Complete**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors to reach completion regardless of success/failure status
 30|
 31|## Constraints
 32|
 33|- Conduct one review at a time. Validate immediately. Never start a second review before first is validated (ensures modular validation, prevents hidden issues)
 34|- Treat user-confirmed reviews as final. Never modify without explicit user permission (maintains stability, prevents unintended changes)
 35|- Check local research using index files when review criteria are unclear. Web search only if local info unavailable. Never review blindly without research (reduces token cost, ensures correct evaluation)
 36|- Place review logs in Logs/Reviewer/ folder with proper categorization. Never create ad-hoc folders or place outside established structure (maintains organization, prevents file chaos)
 37|- Always use popups for yes/no questions. Never use text-only confirmations (ensures clear user intent, prevents miscommunication)
 38|- Always categorize review findings when adding to review documentation. Never place findings uncategorized (maintains organization, enables efficient navigation)
 39|- Never skip compliance verification. Always verify adherence to Executor rules and standards before concluding review (ensures quality, prevents rule violations)
 40|- Never modify code directly during review (reviewer role only, prevents scope drift into implementation)
 41|- Never skip best practices evaluation. Always assess code against industry standards and established patterns (ensures quality, prevents suboptimal solutions)
 42|- Never perform actions outside workflow scope. Always follow defined review processes and never perform tasks outside the current workflow scope unless explicitly requested by the user (prevents token waste, ensures focused execution)
 43|- Never create documentation files unless specifically requested. Never create README.md, CHANGELOG.md, or other documentation files unless specifically requested by the user (prevents token waste, maintains workflow scope discipline)
 44|- Never run subagents unless explicitly requested by the user. Always perform research and analysis using direct tools (web_search, grep, read, etc.) unless user specifically requests subagent delegation (prevents unexpected subagent usage, maintains user control over execution)
 45|
 46|## Architecture
 47|
 48|- Quality-first architecture: Review ensures code quality before implementation proceeds (maintains quality standards, enables early issue detection)
 49|- Modular compliance verification: Each function reviewed for modularity, testability, and best practices adherence (maintains code quality, prevents technical debt)
 50|- Comprehensive scanning: Line-by-line examination of all files within scope (ensures complete coverage, prevents hidden issues)
 51|- Constructive feedback: Specific, actionable recommendations with clear improvement paths (maintains review effectiveness, enables continuous improvement)
 52|
 53|## Tool Configuration
 54|
 55|- Directory verification: `ls -la <directory>` (verify directory structure exists)
 56|- File discovery: `find <path -name "*.md"` (find markdown governance files)
 57|- Pattern search: `grep -r "pattern" <directory>` (search for patterns in rule files)
 58|- JSON validation: `python -m json.tool <file>` (validate JSON syntax, exit code indicates success/failure)
 59|- File comparison: `diff <file1> <file2>` (compare files before changes, exit code 0 = identical)
 60|
 61|## Project Structure
 62|
 63|- `App/` â€“ Application code to review (READ for quality and compliance verification)
 64|- `Plans/` â€“ Implementation plans to review (READ for quality and completeness)
 65|- `Workflow/` â€“ Workflow definitions to review (READ for process compliance)
 66|- `Rules/` â€“ Rule definitions to reference (READ for compliance verification)
 67|- `Docs/` â€“ Documentation to review (READ for completeness and accuracy)
 68|- `Logs/Reviewer/` â€“ Reviewer-specific logs and review records (WRITE review logs here)
 69|
 70|## Workflow
 71|- **Main Workflow**: Workflow/Reviewer/Reviewer_Review_Workflow.md (comprehensive review process)
 72|- **Best Practice Scanner**: Workflow/Reviewer/Reviewer_Best_Practice_Scanner_Workflow.md (App/ directory compliance scanning)
 73|- **Quality Framework**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Quality_Assessment_Framework.md (review quality assessment)
 74|- **Validation Patterns**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Validation_Enforcement_Patterns.md (review verification)
 75|
 76|## Modular Compliance Review Rules
 77|
 78|### Function-by-Function Verification
 79|- **DO**: Verify each function follows single responsibility principle
 80|- **DO**: Check that functions have clear inputs and outputs
 81|- **DO**: Ensure functions are independently testable
 82|- **DO**: Verify dependency injection usage for testability
 83|- **DO**: Check separation of business logic from I/O operations
 84|- **DON'T**: Accept monolithic functions that do multiple things
 85|- **DON'T**: Overlook hardcoded dependencies that should be injected
 86|- **DON'T**: Ignore mixed business logic and I/O operations
 87|
 88|### Testing Requirements Verification
 89|- **DO**: Verify tests exist for each function in Scripts/Tests/
 90|- **DO**: Check that tests are placed in correct directory (not App/)
 91|- **DO**: Ensure tests use dependency injection and mocking
 92|- **DO**: Verify test coverage meets plan requirements (â‰¥90%)
 93|- **DO**: Check that both success and error paths are tested
 94|- **DON'T**: Accept missing tests for any function
 95|- **DON'T**: Overlook tests placed in App/ directory
 96|- **DON'T**: Ignore tests that depend on external systems without mocking
 97|
 98|### Code Quality Standards Verification
 99|- **DO**: Verify code follows project coding standards and conventions
100|- **DO**: Check for appropriate error handling and validation
101|- **DO**: Ensure code is readable and maintainable
102|- **DO**: Verify security best practices adherence
103|- **DO**: Check for meaningful comments where necessary
104|- **DON'T**: Accept code that is difficult to understand
105|- **DON'T**: Overlook missing error handling and validation
106|- **DON'T**: Ignore insecure coding practices
107|
108|### Best Practices Evaluation
109|- **DO**: Evaluate code against industry best practices
110|- **DO**: Check for established design patterns
111|- **DO**: Verify adherence to SOLID principles
112|- **DO**: Assess code for testability and maintainability
113|- **DO**: Check for proper separation of concerns
114|- **DON'T**: Accept anti-patterns or poor practices
115|- **DON'T**: Overlook violations of established principles
116|- **DON'T**: Ignore maintainability concerns
117|
118|## Review Quality Rules
119|
120|### Comprehensive Coverage
121|- **DO**: Review all files within scope line by line
122|- **DO**: Ensure no files are skipped during review
123|- **DO**: Verify complete coverage of review criteria
124|- **DO**: Check that all compliance rules are evaluated
125|- **DON'T**: Skip files during review process
126|- **DON'T**: Perform partial reviews when comprehensive is required
127|- **DON'T**: Overlook any compliance verification steps
128|
129|### Constructive Feedback
130|- **DO**: Provide specific, actionable feedback
131|- **DO**: Include clear improvement recommendations
132|- **DO**: Reference specific code sections with line numbers
133|- **DO**: Explain the reasoning behind findings
134|- **DON'T**: Provide vague or general feedback
135|- **DON'T** Make subjective judgments without evidence
136|- **DON'T** Issue feedback without clear improvement paths
137|
138|### Documentation Standards
139|- **DO**: Document all review findings comprehensively
140|- **DO**: Include severity ratings for issues found
141|- **DO**: Provide context for why issues matter
142|- **DO** Maintain clear review logs with timestamps
143|- **DON'T** Skip documentation of review findings
144|- **DON'T** Leave findings without proper categorization
145|- **DON'T** Omit context or rationale for recommendations
146|
147|## Subagent Usage for Large-Scale Scanning
148|
149|### Subagent Prompting Strategy
150|- **DO**: Use subagents for large-scale App/ directory scanning when explicitly requested
151|- **DO**: Provide precise, detailed prompts with clear scope and criteria
152|- **DO**: Define specific compliance rules to check (modularity, testing, best practices)
153|- **DO**: Specify exact output format and structure expected
154|- **DO** Include clear boundaries and deliverable expectations
155|- **DON'T**: Use vague or ambiguous subagent prompts
156|- **DON'T** Skip defining exact scope and evaluation criteria
157|- **DON'T** Accept subagent results without validation
158|
159|### Subagent Coordination
160|- **DO**: Break large scanning tasks into logical chunks (by module, directory, or complexity)
161|- **DO**: Use parallel subagents for independent scanning tasks
162|- **DO**: Validate subagent results against established criteria
163|- **DO**: Consolidate subagent findings into comprehensive report
164|- **DON'T** Create overlapping subagent scopes that cause redundancy
165|- **DON'T** Accept subagent findings without cross-validation
166|- **DON'T** Skip consolidation and verification of subagent results
167|
168|## Current Status
169|
170|**Rules**: Initial version based on code review best practices and quality assurance standards
171|**Categories**: Modular compliance, code quality, best practices evaluation, comprehensive coverage, constructive feedback
172|**Enforcement**: Quality verification (primary), compliance standards (secondary), best practices evaluation (tertiary)
173|**Modular Compliance**: Function-by-function verification against Executor rules with subagent support for large-scale scanning
</file-view>

  9|# Architect General Workflow
 10|
 11|**ID**: WF-ARCH-001  
 12|**Owner**: Architect Agent  
 13|**Frequency**: Per architectural task  
 14|**Duration**: Variable (task-dependent)  
 15|**Priority**: High
 16|**Workflow Type**: Continuous Operation
 17|**Execution Modes**: Manual, Auto, Complete
 18|
 19|## Purpose
 20|Systematic architectural decision-making ensuring infrastructure design follows best practices and maintains compliance with governance rules, enforced through the validation-based governance system for automatic permission validation and audit logging.
 21|
 22|## Roles and Owners
 23|- **Architect Agent**: Executes workflow steps, enforces governance rules
 24|- **User**: Provides task requirements, approves decisions
 25|- **Governance System**: Automatic enforcement via validation system (non-manual)
 26|
 27|## Trigger and End State
 28|- **Trigger**: User requests architectural work or agent initiates task
 29|- **End State**: Implementation complete, documented, verified for compliance
 30|
 31|## Workflow Steps (93 steps)
 32|### Phase 0. Read Architect Rules
 33|- 1. Read Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md to load current governance constraints
 34|- 2. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md to understand terminology definitions
 35|- 3. Parse YAML frontmatter and rule definitions for implementation guidance
 36|- 4. Store rule context for reference throughout workflow execution
 37|- 5. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
 38|- 6. **PRINT** "Architect rules loaded from Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md"
 39|
 40|### Phase 1. Select Execution Mode
 41|- 7. Ask user to select execution mode for this workflow using popup menu (see Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md for execution mode definitions)
 42|- 8. Store selected execution mode for failure handling throughout workflow
 43|- 9. **PRINT** "Execution mode selected - [Manual/Auto/Complete] will govern failure handling"
 44|
 45|### Phase 2. Architect Interaction
 46|- 10. Ask user: "Hi, Architect here - how can I help you today?"
 47|- 11. Wait for user to specify their architectural task or question
 48|- 12. Clarify the task if needed
 49|- 13. Review user request and check local research using index files before web search
 50|- 14. Apply loaded architect rules to task requirements
 51|- 15. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply execution mode handling patterns (see Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md)
 52|- 16. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_2_complete"
 53|- 17. **PRINT** "Initiating architect interaction - awaiting user task specification"
 54|
 55|### Phase 3. Research Best Practices
 56|- 18. Check code documentation (Docs/Code/) for examples relevant to the specific type of code being implemented (Python, JSON, YAML, Bash, etc.)
 57|- 19. **BEST PRACTICES WEB SEARCH**: Web search must be performed before major architectural decisions (per Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md). Research industry standards and established patterns for the architectural approach being considered.
 58|- 20. Gather multiple approaches and patterns from web search and local research
 59|- 21. Ensure proposed solutions comply with governance rules
 60|- 22. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply execution mode handling patterns (see Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md)
 61|- 23. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_3_complete"

# Architect General Workflow

**ID**: WF-ARCH-001  
**Owner**: Architect Agent  
**Frequency**: Per architectural task  
**Duration**: Variable (task-dependent)  
**Priority**: High
**Workflow Type**: Continuous Operation
**Execution Modes**: Manual, Auto, Complete

- **Architect Agent**: Executes workflow steps, enforces governance rules
- **User**: Provides task requirements, approves decisions

# Architect General Workflow

**ID**: WF-ARCH-001  
**Owner**: Architect Agent  
**Frequency**: Per architectural task  
**Duration**: Variable (task-dependent)  
**Priority**: High
**Workflow Type**: Continuous Operation
**Execution Modes**: Manual, Auto, Complete

## Purpose
Systematic architectural decision-making ensuring infrastructure design follows best practices and maintains compliance with governance rules, enforced through the validation-based governance system for automatic permission validation and audit logging.

## Roles and Owners
- **Architect Agent**: Executes workflow steps, enforces governance rules
- **User**: Provides task requirements, approves decisions
- **Governance System**: Automatic enforcement via validation system (non-manual)

## Trigger and End State
- **Trigger**: User requests architectural work or agent initiates task
- **End State**: Implementation complete, documented, verified for compliance

## Workflow Steps (93 steps)
### Phase 0. Read Architect Rules
- 1. Read Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md to load current governance constraints
- 2. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md to understand terminology definitions
- 3. Parse YAML frontmatter and rule definitions for implementation guidance
- 4. Store rule context for reference throughout workflow execution
- 5. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
- 6. **PRINT** "Architect rules loaded from Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md"

### Phase 1. Select Execution Mode
- 7. Ask user to select execution mode for this workflow using popup menu (see Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md for execution mode definitions)
- 8. Store selected execution mode for failure handling throughout workflow
- 9. **PRINT** "Execution mode selected - [Manual/Auto/Complete] will govern failure handling"

### Phase 2. Architect Interaction
- 10. Ask user: "Hi, Architect here - how can I help you today?"
- 11. Wait for user to specify their architectural task or question
- 12. Clarify the task if needed
- 13. Review user request and check local research using index files before web search
- 14. Apply loaded architect rules to task requirements
- 15. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply execution mode handling patterns (see Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md)
- 16. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_2_complete"
- 17. **PRINT** "Initiating architect interaction - awaiting user task specification"

### Phase 3. Research Best Practices
- 18. Check code documentation (Docs/Code/) for examples relevant to the specific type of code being implemented (Python, JSON, YAML, Bash, etc.)
- 19. **BEST PRACTICES WEB SEARCH**: Web search must be performed before major architectural decisions (per Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md). Research industry standards and established patterns for the architectural approach being considered.
- 20. Gather multiple approaches and patterns from web search and local research
- 21. Ensure proposed solutions comply with governance rules
- 22. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply execution mode handling patterns (see Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md)
- 23. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_3_complete"
- 24. **PRINT** "Researching best practices - checking code documentation for relevant examples"
- 25. **PRINT** "Best practices web search initiated - required before major architectural decisions"
- 26. **PRINT** "Research complete - gathered multiple implementation approaches from industry standards"

### Phase 4. Generate Options
- 27. Generate 2-4 implementation options based on research
- 28. **VALIDATION**: Validate options against viable option criteria (see Workflow/Architect/Reference/Option_Evaluation_Framework.md)
- 29. **ARCHITECT OPINION**: Provide analysis and recommendation BEFORE user selection
- 30. **PRESENTATION PATTERN**: Present options with metrics, provide architect opinion, use popup menu for selection
- 31. **RULE ENFORCEMENT**: Ensure options comply with Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md
- 32. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply execution mode handling patterns (see Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md)
- 33. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_4_complete"
- 34. **PRINT**: "Generating implementation options - applying viable option criteria"
- 35. **PRINT**: "Options generated - presenting with impact, effort, and risk metrics"
- 36. **PRINT**: "Architect opinion provided - recommending optimal approach based on analysis"

### Phase 5. Specify Implementation
- 37. Create detailed specification for selected approach
- 38. **SPECIFICATION CONFIRMATION**: Ask user to confirm specification or request modifications using popup menu with [Confirm/Modify] options
- 39. **VALIDATION**: Validate specification completeness and compliance (see Workflow/Architect/Reference/Option_Evaluation_Framework.md)
- 40. **IMPLEMENTATION MODE SELECTION**: Ask user to choose using popup menu (see Workflow/Architect/Reference/Implementation_Mode_Patterns.md)
- 41. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply execution mode handling patterns (see Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md)
- 42. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_5_complete"
- 43. **PRINT** "Creating detailed implementation specification - defining architecture and constraints"
- 44. **PRINT** "Specification complete - verifying file placement compliance with directory structure"
- 45. **PRINT** "Implementation mode selection presented - awaiting user choice between automated and manual modes"

### Phase 6. Implement (One Function at a Time)
- 46. Build exactly one function at a time, test immediately
- 47. Present function and test result to user after each successful test
- 48. Wait for explicit user confirmation before proceeding
- 49. Treat user-confirmed functions as locked
- **AUTOMATED PROGRESSION NOTE**: The validation system allows state-mutating tools (edit, write, exec) automatically during this step. User confirmation requests use ask_user_question (unvalidated) to pause for approval without triggering failure intervention.
- 50. When placing files, check INDEX.md for folder structure (token-efficient vs loading full directory)
- 51. Load Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md only when specific constraints are needed
- 52. When function fails, apply selected execution mode (see Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md)
- 53. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_6_in_progress" during implementation, "phase_6_complete" when finished
- 54. **PRINT**: "Implementing function - building one function at a time per architect rules"
- 55. **PRINT**: "Function test complete - presenting test results to user for confirmation"
- 56. **PRINT**: "Awaiting user confirmation - treating function as locked once confirmed"
- 57. **PRINT**: "Function implementation complete - proceeding to next function"

### Phase 7. Verify Compliance
- 58. Verify implementation matches specification
- 59. Run verification tests
- 60. Ensure constitutional compliance per Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md
- 61. Never skip compliance checks
- 62. Always verify architectural compliance before proceeding
- 63. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply execution mode handling patterns (see Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md)
- 64. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_7_complete"
- 65. **PRINT**: "Verifying compliance - checking implementation against specification"
- 66. **PRINT**: "Running verification tests - ensuring all success criteria met"
- 67. **PRINT**: "Constitutional compliance verified - implementation aligns with architect rules"
- 68. **PRINT**: "Architectural compliance complete - ready to proceed"

### Phase 8. Document
- 69. Update relevant governance files for the agent being worked on:
  - INDEX.md (if new folders are created)
  - Rules/{Agent}/{Agent}_Rules.md (if new rules are added)
  - Workflow/Templates/Workflow_Template.md (if template changes)
  - AGENTS.md (if agent capabilities change)

- 71. Never place files uncategorized

- 73. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_8_complete"
- 74. **PRINT**: "Updating governance documentation - modifying relevant agent files"
- 75. **PRINT**: "Documentation categorization verified - all files properly categorized per architect rules"
- 76. **PRINT**: "Documentation complete - governance files updated"

### Phase 9. Final Validation
- 77. Verify implementation matches intended scope for the specific area:
  - Rules: Follow template and proper formatting
  - Workflow: Follow structure and is executable
  - Scripts: Function as intended
  - Documentation: Properly categorized
- 78. Confirm governance file placement compliance per INDEX.md
- 79. Validate no unintended changes outside the target area
  - Run git status to check for changes
  - If unintended changes detected, present popup menu with [Accept Changes/Restore Files] options
  - Only attempt restore after user explicitly selects "Restore Files" option
- 80. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply execution mode handling patterns (see Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md)
- 81. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_9_complete"
- 82. **PRINT**: "Final validation initiated - verifying implementation scope compliance"
- 83. **PRINT**: "Rules verification complete - template and formatting validated"
- 84. **PRINT**: "Workflow verification complete - structure and executability confirmed"
- 85. **PRINT**: "Scripts verification complete - functionality validated"
- 86. **PRINT**: "Documentation verification complete - categorization confirmed"
- 87. **PRINT**: "Governance file placement verified - compliance with INDEX.md confirmed"
- 88. **PRINT**: "Unintended changes check complete - no changes outside target area detected"

421|def extract_frontmatter(file_path: Path) -> Optional[Dict]:
422|    """Extract YAML frontmatter from markdown file."""
423|    try:
424|        with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
425|            content = f.read()
426|        
427|        # Check for YAML frontmatter (--- delimited)
428|        if content.startswith('---'):
429|            frontmatter_end = content.find('---', 3)
430|            if frontmatter_end != -1:
431|                frontmatter_str = content[3:frontmatter_end].strip()
432|                return yaml.safe_load(frontmatter_str)
433|        
434|        return None
435|    except Exception as e:
436|        print(f"Error extracting frontmatter from {file_path}: {e}")
437|        return None
438|
439|def determine_schema_type(file_path: Path) -> Optional[str]:
440|    """Determine which schema to use based on file path and name."""
441|    path_str = str(file_path).lower()
442|    
443|    # Workflow files
444|    if 'workflow' in path_str and file_path.suffix == '.md':
445|        return 'workflow'
446|    
447|    # Rules files
448|    if 'rules' in path_str and file_path.name.endswith('_rules.md'):
449|        return 'rules'
450|    
451|    # AGENTS.md
452|    if file_path.name == 'agents.md':
453|        return 'agents'
454|    
455|    # Skill files
456|    if 'skill' in path_str and file_path.name == 'SKILL.md':
457|        return 'skill'
458|    
459|    # Reference files
460|    if 'reference' in path_str and file_path.suffix == '.md':
461|        return 'reference'
462|    
463|    # Template files
464|    if 'template' in path_str and file_path.suffix == '.md':
465|        return 'template'
466|    
467|    return None
468|
469|def load_schema(schema_type: str, schema_dir: Path) -> Dict:
470|    """Load JSON schema for given type."""
471|    schema_file = schema_dir / SCHEMA_MAPPING[schema_type]
472|    with open(schema_file, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
473|        return json.load(f)
474|
475|def validate_frontmatter(frontmatter: Dict, schema: Dict) -> Tuple[bool, List[str]]:
476|    """Validate frontmatter against schema using basic validation."""
477|    errors = []
478|    
479|    # Check required fields
480|    required_fields = schema.get('required', [])
481|    for field in required_fields:
482|        if field not in frontmatter:
483|            errors.append(f"Missing required field: {field}")
484|    
485|    # Check field types and patterns
486|    properties = schema.get('properties', {})
487|    for field, field_schema in properties.items():
488|        if field in frontmatter:
489|            value = frontmatter[field]
490|            
491|            # Type validation
492|            expected_type = field_schema.get('type')
493|            if expected_type == 'string' and not isinstance(value, str):
494|                errors.append(f"Field '{field}' should be string, got {type(value).__name__}")

  9|# Architect Consistency Check Workflow
 10|
 11|**ID**: WF-ARCH-CONS-CHECK  
 12|**Owner**: Architect Agent  
 13|**Frequency**: On-demand (recommended: weekly basic, monthly comprehensive)  
 14|**Duration**: Variable (30-90 minutes depending on scope)  
 15|**Priority**: High
 16|**Workflow Type**: Single-Execution (Utility/Tool Workflow)
 17|**Execution Modes**: Full Comprehensive, Basic Essential, Targeted, Quick Check
 18|
 19|## Purpose
 20|Systematic validation of harness architecture consistency across the entire project to identify structural issues, broken references, terminology inconsistencies, governance gaps, and architectural health using advanced fitness functions and multi-agent validation. The workflow continues through all phases even if individual validation steps fail, treating failures as informational for the final report rather than blocking progress.

 23|**Harness Architecture Only**: Governance files, workflows, rules, documentation (excludes /app folder)

 34|- **End State**: Comprehensive consistency report generated in Logs/Architect/Consistency Review/
 35|
 36|## Workflow Steps (176 steps)
 37|
 38|**IMPORTANT**: All phases execute sequentially. Phase validation failures are treated as informational warnings and do not block workflow progression. All findings are aggregated in the final report for comprehensive review.

 40|### Phase 0. Read Architect Rules + Scan Scope
 41|- 1. Read Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md to understand governance constraints
 42|- 2. Read Workflow/Templates/Workflow_Template.md for workflow structure patterns

 45|- 5. Store governance context for reference throughout scan
 46|- 6. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
 47|- 7. **PRINT**: "Architect rules loaded - initiating harness architecture consistency scan"
 48|
 49|### Phase 1. Select Scan Strategy
 50|- 8. Ask user to select scan strategy using popup menu:
</file-view>

  7|---
  8|
  9|# Architect Workflow Template
 10|
 11|**Purpose**: Architect-specific template for creating agent workflows.
 12|
 13|## Template Overview
 14|
 15|This template is used by the Architect agent to create workflows for other agents. All workflows must follow this structure for consistency.
 16|
 17|## Workflow Types
 18|
 19|Architect creates two types of workflows with different Phase 10 patterns:
 20|
 21|### 1. Continuous Operation Workflows (Standard Agent Workflows)
 22|- **Purpose**: Agents that should always be ready for new tasks
 23|- **Phase 10 Pattern**: Include "Return to step 1" for continuous operation
 24|- **Examples**: Architect_General_Workflow, Planner_Plan_Workflow, Executor_Implementation_Cycle
 25|- **Behavior**: Workflow cycles indefinitely, agent always ready for next task
 26|- **Use Case**: Primary agent workflows that handle ongoing agent operations
 27|
 28|### 2. Single-Execution Workflows (Utility/Tool Workflows)
 29|- **Purpose**: Utility workflows that execute once and terminate
 30|- **Phase 10 Pattern**: Exclude or modify to termination (no "Return to step 1")
 31|- **Examples**: Architect_Consistency_Check_Workflow, Architect_Consistency_Fix_Workflow
 32|- **Behavior**: Workflow executes once and terminates, no automatic looping
 33|- **Use Case**: Specialized workflows that run on-demand and complete
 34|
 35|### Workflow Type Selection Guidelines
 36|- **Use Continuous Operation**: For primary agent workflows that should always be available
 37|- **Use Single-Execution**: For utility workflows, validation workflows, maintenance workflows
 38|
 39|## Template Reference
 40|
 41|- **Location**: Workflow/Templates/Workflow_Template.md
 42|- **Owner**: Architect Agent
 43|- **Usage**: Architect uses this template to create workflows for all agents
 44|- **Updates**: Only Architect should modify this template
 45|
 46|## Template Structure
 47|
 48|## Workflow Header
 49|```markdown
 50|# {Agent} {WorkflowType} Workflow
 51|
 52|**ID**: WF-{AGENT}-{XXX}  
 53|**Owner**: {Agent} Agent  
 54|**Frequency**: {Frequency}  
 55|**Duration**: {Duration}  
 56|**Priority**: {Priority}
 57|**Execution Modes**: {Workflow-specific execution mode options}
 58|
 59|## Purpose
 60|{What this workflow accomplishes and why it exists}
 61|
 62|## Roles and Owners
 63|- **{Agent} Agent**: Executes workflow steps, enforces governance rules
 64|- **User**: Provides task requirements, approves decisions
 65|- **Governance System**: Validation and compliance enforcement
 66|
 67|## Trigger and End State
 68|- **Trigger**: {What triggers this workflow}
 69|- **End State**: {What constitutes workflow completion}
 70|
 71|## Workflow Steps ({total steps} steps)
 72|### Phase 0. Read {Agent} Rules
 73|- 1. Read Rules/{Agent}/{Agent}_Rules.md to load current governance constraints
 74|- 2. Parse YAML frontmatter and rule definitions for implementation guidance
 75|- 3. Store rule context for reference throughout workflow execution
 76|- 4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
 77|- 5. **PRINT** "{Agent} rules loaded from Rules/{Agent}/{Agent}_Rules.md"
 78|
 79|### Phase 1. Select Execution Mode (Workflow-Specific)
 80|- 6. Ask user to select execution mode for this workflow using popup menu:
 81|  - **Workflow-Specific Options**: Each workflow defines its own execution mode options based on its operational needs
 82|  - **Common Patterns**: 
 83|    - Manual/Auto/Complete (traditional phase-based workflows)
 84|    - Manual/Manual Batched/Automatic Batched (file/item processing workflows)
 85|    - Custom modes defined by workflow requirements
 86|- 7. Store selected execution mode for failure handling throughout workflow
 87|- 8. **PRINT** "Execution mode selected - [workflow-specific modes] will govern failure handling"
 88|
 89|### Phase 2. {Agent} Interaction
 90|- 9. Ask user: "Hi, {Agent} here - how can I help you today?"
 91|- 10. Wait for user to specify their task or question
 92|- 11. Clarify the task if needed
 93|- 12. Review user request and check local research using index files before web search
 94|- 13. Apply loaded {agent} rules to task requirements
 95|- 14. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply execution mode handling patterns (see Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md)
 96|- 15. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_2_complete"
 97|- 16. **PRINT** "Initiating {agent} interaction - awaiting user task specification"
 98|
 99|### Phase 3. Research Best Practices
100|- 17. Check code documentation (Docs/Code/) for examples relevant to the specific type of work
</file-view>
```

# Architect Consistency Fix Workflow

**ID**: WF-ARCH-CONS-FIX  
**Owner**: Architect Agent  
**Frequency**: On-demand (triggered after consistency check identifies issues)  
**Duration**: Variable (30-120 minutes depending on issue count and complexity)  
**Priority**: High
**Workflow Type**: Single-Execution (Utility/Tool Workflow)
**Execution Modes**: Manual, Automatic

## Purpose
Systematic resolution of consistency issues identified by the Consistency Check Workflow. This workflow processes the consistency report and implements fixes for broken references, terminology inconsistencies, workflow structure issues, and schema validation problems. The workflow supports both Manual mode (user confirmation for each fix) and Automatic mode (batch processing of non-critical fixes).

## Scope
**Harness Architecture Only**: Governance files, workflows, rules, documentation (excludes /app folder)

**Input**: Consistency report from Logs/Architect/Consistency Review/

**Output**: Fixed governance files and updated consistency report with (FIXED) prefix

## Roles and Owners
- **Architect Agent**: Executes fixes, validates changes, updates governance files
- **User**: Reviews proposed fixes (Manual mode), approves critical changes, validates results
- **Governance System**: Validation and compliance enforcement

## Trigger and End State
- **Trigger**: Consistency check identifies issues requiring fixes
- **End State**: All identified consistency issues resolved, schema validation passing

## Workflow Steps (45 steps)

### Phase 0. Read Architect Rules + Consistency Report
- 1. Read Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md to understand governance constraints
- 2. Read Workflow/Templates/Workflow_Template.md for workflow structure patterns
- 3. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md to understand terminology definitions
- 4. Read most recent consistency report from Logs/Architect/Consistency Review/
- 5. Parse consistency report to identify issues by severity (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW)
- 6. Store governance context and issue list for reference throughout workflow execution
- 7. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
- 8. **PRINT**: "Architect rules and consistency report loaded - {N} issues identified"

### Phase 1. Select Execution Mode
- 9. Ask user to select execution mode using popup menu:
  - **Manual**: Review and approve each fix individually (recommended for CRITICAL issues)
  - **Automatic**: Apply all non-critical fixes automatically, CRITICAL fixes require approval
- 10. Store selected execution mode for failure handling throughout workflow
- 11. **PRINT**: "Execution mode selected - [Manual/Automatic] will govern fix application"

### Phase 2. Issue Categorization and Prioritization
- 12. Categorize identified issues by type:
  - File reference issues (broken paths, missing files)
  - Terminology inconsistencies (outdated terms)
  - Workflow structure issues (missing sections, incorrect formatting)
  - Schema validation issues (categorization rule violations)
- 13. Prioritize issues by severity: CRITICAL > HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW
- 14. Group related issues for batch processing (e.g., all file reference fixes together)
- 15. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_2_complete"
- 16. **PRINT**: "Issues categorized and prioritized - {N} CRITICAL, {N} HIGH, {N} MEDIUM, {N} LOW"

### Phase 3. File Reference Fixes (CRITICAL)
- 17. **SCAN**: For each file reference issue:
  - **Manual Mode**: Present issue details and proposed fix to user via popup menu
  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply fix automatically if LOW/MEDIUM, CRITICAL requires approval
- 18. Fix Workflow_Template.md location references (update to Workflow/Templates/)
- 19. Fix missing or incorrectly named workflow files (rename or create)
- 20. Remove workflow references from rules files (architectural principle compliance)
- 21. Remove references to non-existent rules files
- 22. **VALIDATION**: Validate each fix using file existence checks
- 23. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_3_complete"
- 24. **PRINT**: "File reference fixes complete - {N} references updated"

### Phase 4. Terminology Fixes (HIGH)
- 25. **SCAN**: For each terminology inconsistency:
  - **Manual Mode**: Present term and proposed replacement via popup menu
  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply standard terminology replacements automatically
- 26. Replace outdated "gate" terminology with "validation" (excluding tool names)
- 27. Standardize agent naming conventions
- 28. Ensure consistent framework naming
- 29. **VALIDATION**: Validate terminology fixes using grep to confirm replacements
- 30. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_4_complete"
- 31. **PRINT**: "Terminology fixes complete - {N} terms standardized"

### Phase 5. Workflow Structure Fixes (MEDIUM)
- 32. **SCAN**: For each workflow structure issue:
  - **Manual Mode**: Present structure issue and proposed fix via popup menu
  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply template compliance fixes automatically
- 33. Add missing "Execution Modes" to workflow headers
- 34. Fix step numbering inconsistencies
- 35. Ensure all workflows have mandated sections (header, universal framework references)
- 36. Validate workflow follows template structure
- 37. **VALIDATION**: Validate structure fixes using template comparison
- 38. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_5_complete"
- 39. **PRINT**: "Workflow structure fixes complete - {N} workflows updated"

### Phase 6. Schema Validation Fixes (MEDIUM)
- 40. **SCAN**: For each schema validation issue:
  - **Manual Mode**: Present categorization rule violation and proposed fix via popup menu
  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply categorization rule updates automatically
- 41. Update categorization rules in Scripts/Schema/validate_schemas.py
- 42. Remove index.md exceptions if not required by architecture
- 43. Update rule files to reference correct documentation paths
- 44. **VALIDATION**: Run schema validation script to confirm all fixes
- 45. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_6_complete"
- 46. **PRINT**: "Schema validation fixes complete - validation passing"

### Phase 7. Final Validation and Report Update
- 47. Run comprehensive schema validation: `python Scripts/Schema/validate_schemas.py`
- 48. Run consistency check workflow to verify all issues resolved
- 49. Rename original consistency report with (FIXED) prefix
- 50. Generate summary of fixes applied with before/after comparison
- 51. **VALIDATION**: Validate all fixes completed successfully
- 52. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_7_complete"
- 53. **PRINT**: "Final validation complete - all consistency issues resolved"

### Phase 8. Documentation
- 54. Update AGENTS.md if agent capabilities changed during fixes
- 75. Update INDEX.md if governance structure changed
- 56. Document architectural decisions made during fix process
- 57. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_8_complete"
- 58. **PRINT**: "Documentation complete - governance files updated"

### Phase 9. Final Validation
- 59. Verify all fixes comply with Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md
- 60. Verify schema validation passes (645/645 files)
- 61. Verify no unintended changes outside target files
- 62. **VALIDATION**: Validate that final validation completed successfully
- 63. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_9_complete"
- 64. **PRINT**: "Final validation complete - architecture fully compliant"

### Phase 10. Terminate
- 65. **PRINT**: "Consistency fix workflow complete - {N} issues resolved, schema validation passing"
- 66. **TERMINATE**: End workflow execution (do not return to step 1)

---

purpose: Workflow for Architect agent to systematically fix consistency issues identified in consistency checks
---

# Architect Consistency Fix Workflow

**ID**: WF-ARCH-CONS-FIX  
**Owner**: Architect Agent  
**Frequency**: On-demand (triggered after consistency check identifies issues)  
**Duration**: Variable (30-120 minutes depending on issue count and complexity)  
**Priority**: High
**Workflow Type**: Single-Execution (Utility/Tool Workflow)
**Execution Modes**: Manual, Automatic

## Purpose
Systematic resolution of consistency issues identified by the Consistency Check Workflow. This workflow processes the consistency report and implements fixes for broken references, terminology inconsistencies, workflow structure issues, and schema validation problems. The workflow supports both Manual mode (user confirmation for each fix) and Automatic mode (batch processing of non-critical fixes).

## Scope
**Harness Architecture Only**: Governance files, workflows, rules, documentation (excludes /app folder)

**Input**: Consistency report from Logs/Architect/Consistency Review/

**Output**: Fixed governance files and updated consistency report with (FIXED) prefix

## Roles and Owners
- **Architect Agent**: Executes fixes, validates changes, updates governance files
- **User**: Reviews proposed fixes (Manual mode), approves critical changes, validates results
- **Governance System**: Validation and compliance enforcement

## Trigger and End State
- **Trigger**: Consistency check identifies issues requiring fixes
- **End State**: All identified consistency issues resolved, schema validation passing

## Workflow Steps (65 steps)

### Phase 0. Read Architect Rules + Consistency Report
- 1. Read Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md to understand governance constraints
- 2. Read Workflow/Templates/Workflow_Template.md for workflow structure patterns
- 3. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md to understand terminology definitions
- 4. Read most recent consistency report from Logs/Architect/Consistency Review/
- 5. Parse consistency report to identify issues by severity (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW)
- 6. Store governance context and issue list for reference throughout workflow execution
- 7. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
- 8. **PRINT**: "Architect rules and consistency report loaded - {N} issues identified"

### Phase 1. Select Execution Mode
- 9. Ask user to select execution mode using popup menu:
  - **Manual**: Review and approve each fix individually (recommended for CRITICAL issues)
  - **Automatic**: Apply all non-critical fixes automatically, CRITICAL fixes require approval
- 10. Store selected execution mode for failure handling throughout workflow
- 11. **PRINT**: "Execution mode selected - [Manual/Automatic] will govern fix application"

### Phase 2. Issue Categorization and Prioritization
- 12. Categorize identified issues by type:
  - File reference issues (broken paths, missing files)
  - Terminology inconsistencies (outdated terms)
  - Workflow structure issues (missing sections, incorrect formatting)
  - Schema validation issues (categorization rule violations)
- 13. Prioritize issues by severity: CRITICAL > HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW
- 14. Group related issues for batch processing (e.g., all file reference fixes together)
- 15. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_2_complete"
- 16. **PRINT**: "Issues categorized and prioritized - {N} CRITICAL, {N} HIGH, {N} MEDIUM, {N} LOW"

### Phase 3. File Reference Fixes (CRITICAL)
- 17. **SCAN**: For each file reference issue:
  - **Manual Mode**: Present issue details and proposed fix to user via popup menu
  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply fix automatically if LOW/MEDIUM, CRITICAL requires approval
- 18. Fix Workflow_Template.md location references (update to Workflow/Templates/)
- 19. Fix missing or incorrectly named workflow files (rename or create)
- 20. Remove workflow references from rules files (architectural principle compliance)
- 21. Remove references to non-existent rules files
- 22. **VALIDATION**: Validate each fix using file existence checks
- 23. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_3_complete"
- 24. **PRINT**: "File reference fixes complete - {N} references updated"

### Phase 4. Terminology Fixes (HIGH)
- 25. **SCAN**: For each terminology inconsistency:
  - **Manual Mode**: Present term and proposed replacement via popup menu
  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply standard terminology replacements automatically
- 26. Replace outdated "gate" terminology with "validation" (excluding tool names)
- 27. Standardize agent naming conventions
- 28. Ensure consistent framework naming
- 29. **VALIDATION**: Validate terminology fixes using grep to confirm replacements
- 30. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_4_complete"
- 31. **PRINT**: "Terminology fixes complete - {N} terms standardized"

### Phase 5. Workflow Structure Fixes (MEDIUM)
- 32. **SCAN**: For each workflow structure issue:
  - **Manual Mode**: Present structure issue and proposed fix via popup menu
  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply template compliance fixes automatically
- 33. Add missing "Execution Modes" to workflow headers
- 34. Fix step numbering inconsistencies
- 35. Ensure all workflows have mandated sections (header, universal framework references)
- 36. Validate workflow follows template structure
- 37. **VALIDATION**: Validate structure fixes using template comparison
- 38. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_5_complete"
- 39. **PRINT**: "Workflow structure fixes complete - {N} workflows updated"

### Phase 6. Schema Validation Fixes (MEDIUM)
- 40. **SCAN**: For each schema validation issue:
  - **Manual Mode**: Present categorization rule violation and proposed fix via popup menu
  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply categorization rule updates automatically
- 41. Update categorization rules in Scripts/Schema/validate_schemas.py
- 42. Remove index.md exceptions if not required by architecture
- 43. Update rule files to reference correct documentation paths
- 44. **VALIDATION**: Run schema validation script to confirm all fixes
- 45. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_6_complete"
- 46. **PRINT**: "Schema validation fixes complete - validation passing"

### Phase 7. Final Validation and Report Update
- 47. Run comprehensive schema validation: `python Scripts/Schema/validate_schemas.py`
- 48. Run consistency check workflow to verify all issues resolved
- 49. Rename original consistency report with (FIXED) prefix
- 50. Generate summary of fixes applied with before/after comparison
- 51. **VALIDATION**: Validate all fixes completed successfully
- 52. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_7_complete"
- 53. **PRINT**: "Final validation complete - all consistency issues resolved"

### Phase 8. Documentation
- 54. Update AGENTS.md if agent capabilities changed during fixes
- 55. Update INDEX.md if governance structure changed
- 56. Document architectural decisions made during fix process
- 57. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_8_complete"
- 58. **PRINT**: "Documentation complete - governance files updated"

### Phase 9. Final Validation
- 59. Verify all fixes comply with Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md
- 60. Verify schema validation passes (645/645 files)
- 61. Verify no unintended changes outside target files
- 62. **VALIDATION**: Validate that final validation completed successfully
- 63. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_9_complete"
- 64. **PRINT**: "Final validation complete - architecture fully compliant"

### Phase 10. Terminate
- 65. **PRINT**: "Consistency fix workflow complete - {N} issues resolved, schema validation passing"
- 66. **TERMINATE**: End workflow execution (do not return to step 1)

---

- **Architect Customization**: Consistency fix quality criteria
- **Focus**: Fix accuracy and architectural compliance

### Role Responsibilities

- **Focus**: Issue resolution efficiency and accuracy

- **Architect Customization**: Consistency fix state tracking
- **Focus**: Fix progress state and validation tracking

### Execution Strategy
- **Universal Framework**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Execution_Strategy_Guidelines.md
- **Architect Customization**: Manual vs Automatic fix execution patterns
- **Focus**: Prioritized issue resolution and user approval handling

### Validation Enforcement
- **Universal Framework**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Validation_Enforcement_Patterns.md
- **Architect Customization**: Fix validation patterns
- **Focus**: Schema validation and architectural compliance verification

### Runtime Prerequisites
- **Universal Framework**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Runtime_Prerequisites.md

- **Focus**: Runtime paths and infrastructure requirements for fix execution

### Workflow Template

- **Architect Customization**: Template compliance validation during fixes
- **Focus**: Ensuring governance files maintain template compliance

## File Placement Compliance

- Place workflow file in Workflow/Architect/Architect_Consistency_Fix_Workflow.md
- Follow naming convention: {Agent}_{WorkflowType}_Workflow.md
- Check INDEX.md for folder structure compliance

 12|**Owner**: Architect Agent  
 13|**Frequency**: On-demand (triggered after consistency check identifies issues)  
 14|**Duration**: Variable (30-120 minutes depending on issue count and complexity)  
 15|**Priority**: High
 16|**Workflow Type**: Single-Execution (Utility/Tool Workflow)
 17|**Execution Modes**: Manual, Automatic
 18|
 19|## Purpose
 20|Systematic resolution of consistency issues identified by the Consistency Check Workflow. This workflow processes the consistency report and implements fixes for broken references, terminology inconsistencies, workflow structure issues, and schema validation problems. The workflow supports both Manual mode (user confirmation for each fix) and Automatic mode (batch processing of non-critical fixes).
 21|
 22|## Scope
 23|**Harness Architecture Only**: Governance files, workflows, rules, documentation (excludes /app folder)
 24|
 25|**Input**: Consistency report from Logs/Architect/Consistency Review/
 26|
 27|**Output**: Fixed governance files and updated consistency report with (FIXED) prefix
 28|
 29|## Roles and Owners
 30|- **Architect Agent**: Executes fixes, validates changes, updates governance files
 31|- **User**: Reviews proposed fixes (Manual mode), approves critical changes, validates results
 32|- **Governance System**: Validation and compliance enforcement
 33|
 34|## Trigger and End State
 35|- **Trigger**: Consistency check identifies issues requiring fixes
 36|- **End State**: All identified consistency issues resolved, schema validation passing
 37|
 38|## Workflow Steps (65 steps)
 39|
 40|### Phase 0. Read Architect Rules + Consistency Report
 41|- 1. Read Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md to understand governance constraints
 42|- 2. Read Workflow/Templates/Workflow_Template.md for workflow structure patterns
 43|- 3. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md to understand terminology definitions
 44|- 4. Read most recent consistency report from Logs/Architect/Consistency Review/
 45|- 5. Parse consistency report to identify issues by severity (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW)
 46|- 6. Store governance context and issue list for reference throughout workflow execution
 47|- 7. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
 48|- 8. **PRINT**: "Architect rules and consistency report loaded - {N} issues identified"
 49|
 50|### Phase 1. Select Execution Mode
 51|- 9. Ask user to select execution mode using popup menu:
 52|  - **Manual**: Review and approve each fix individually (recommended for CRITICAL issues)
 53|  - **Automatic**: Apply all non-critical fixes automatically, CRITICAL fixes require approval
 54|- 10. Store selected execution mode for failure handling throughout workflow
 55|- 11. **PRINT**: "Execution mode selected - [Manual/Automatic] will govern fix application"
 56|
 57|### Phase 2. Issue Categorization and Prioritization
 58|- 12. Categorize identified issues by type:
 59|  - File reference issues (broken paths, missing files)
 60|  - Terminology inconsistencies (outdated terms)
 61|  - Workflow structure issues (missing sections, incorrect formatting)
 62|  - Schema validation issues (categorization rule violations)
 63|- 13. Prioritize issues by severity: CRITICAL > HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW
 64|- 14. Group related issues for batch processing (e.g., all file reference fixes together)
 65|- 15. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_2_complete"
 66|- 16. **PRINT**: "Issues categorized and prioritized - {N} CRITICAL, {N} HIGH, {N} MEDIUM, {N} LOW"
 67|
 68|### Phase 3. File Reference Fixes (CRITICAL)
 69|- 17. **SCAN**: For each file reference issue:
 70|  - **Manual Mode**: Present issue details and proposed fix to user via popup menu
 71|  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply fix automatically if LOW/MEDIUM, CRITICAL requires approval
 72|- 18. Fix Workflow_Template.md location references (update to Workflow/Templates/)
 73|- 19. Fix missing or incorrectly named workflow files (rename or create)
 74|- 20. Remove workflow references from rules files (architectural principle compliance)
 75|- 21. Remove references to non-existent rules files
 76|- 22. **VALIDATION**: Validate each fix using file existence checks
 77|- 23. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_3_complete"
 78|- 24. **PRINT**: "File reference fixes complete - {N} references updated"
 79|
 80|### Phase 4. Terminology Fixes (HIGH)
 81|- 25. **SCAN**: For each terminology inconsistency:
 82|  - **Manual Mode**: Present term and proposed replacement via popup menu
 83|  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply standard terminology replacements automatically
 84|- 26. Replace outdated "gate" terminology with "validation" (excluding tool names)
 85|- 27. Standardize agent naming conventions
 86|- 28. Ensure consistent framework naming
 87|- 29. **VALIDATION**: Validate terminology fixes using grep to confirm replacements
 88|- 30. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_4_complete"
 89|- 31. **PRINT**: "Terminology fixes complete - {N} terms standardized"
 90|
 91|### Phase 5. Workflow Structure Fixes (MEDIUM)
 92|- 32. **SCAN**: For each workflow structure issue:
 93|  - **Manual Mode**: Present structure issue and proposed fix via popup menu
 94|  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply template compliance fixes automatically
 95|- 33. Add missing "Execution Modes" to workflow headers
 96|- 34. Fix step numbering inconsistencies
 97|- 35. Ensure all workflows have mandated sections (header, universal framework references)
 98|- 36. Validate workflow follows template structure
 99|- 37. **VALIDATION**: Validate structure fixes using template comparison
100|- 38. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_5_complete"
101|- 39. **PRINT**: "Workflow structure fixes complete - {N} workflows updated"
102|
103|### Phase 6. Schema Validation Fixes (MEDIUM)
104|- 40. **SCAN**: For each schema validation issue:
105|  - **Manual Mode**: Present categorization rule violation and proposed fix via popup menu
106|  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply categorization rule updates automatically
107|- 41. Update categorization rules in Scripts/Schema/validate_schemas.py
108|- 42. Remove index.md exceptions if not required by architecture
109|- 43. Update rule files to reference correct documentation paths
110|- 44. **VALIDATION**: Run schema validation script to confirm all fixes
111|- 45. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_6_complete"
112|- 46. **PRINT**: "Schema validation fixes complete - validation passing"
113|
114|### Phase 7. Final Validation and Report Update
115|- 47. Run comprehensive schema validation: `python Scripts/Schema/validate_schemas.py`
116|- 48. Run consistency check workflow to verify all issues resolved
117|- 49. Rename original consistency report with (FIXED) prefix
118|- 50. Generate summary of fixes applied with before/after comparison
119|- 51. **VALIDATION**: Validate all fixes completed successfully
120|- 52. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_7_complete"
121|- 53. **PRINT**: "Final validation complete - all consistency issues resolved"
122|
123|### Phase 8. Documentation
124|- 54. Update AGENTS.md if agent capabilities changed during fixes
125|- 55. Update INDEX.md if governance structure changed
126|- 56. Document architectural decisions made during fix process
127|- 57. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_8_complete"
128|- 58. **PRINT**: "Documentation complete - governance files updated"
129|
130|### Phase 9. Final Validation
131|- 59. Verify all fixes comply with Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md
132|- 60. Verify schema validation passes (645/645 files)
133|- 61. Verify no unintended changes outside target files
134|- 62. **VALIDATION**: Validate that final validation completed successfully
135|- 63. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_9_complete"
136|- 64. **PRINT**: "Final validation complete - architecture fully compliant"
137|
138|### Phase 10. Terminate
139|- 65. **PRINT**: "Consistency fix workflow complete - {N} issues resolved, schema validation passing"
140|- 66. **TERMINATE**: End workflow execution (do not return to step 1)
141|

id: wf-arch-cons-fix
status: active
owner: architect-agent
updated: 2026-07-28
purpose: Workflow for Architect agent to systematically fix consistency issues identified in consistency checks
---

# Architect Consistency Fix Workflow

**ID**: WF-ARCH-CONS-FIX  
**Owner**: Architect Agent  
**Frequency**: On-demand (triggered after consistency check identifies issues)  
**Duration**: Variable (30-120 minutes depending on issue count and complexity)  
**Priority**: High
**Workflow Type**: Single-Execution (Utility/Tool Workflow)
**Execution Modes**: Manual, Automatic

## Purpose
Systematic resolution of consistency issues identified by the Consistency Check Workflow. This workflow processes the consistency report and implements fixes for broken references, terminology inconsistencies, workflow structure issues, and schema validation problems. The workflow supports both Manual mode (user confirmation for each fix) and Automatic mode (batch processing of non-critical fixes).

## Scope
**Harness Architecture Only**: Governance files, workflows, rules, documentation (excludes /app folder)

**Input**: Consistency report from Logs/Architect/Consistency Review/

**Output**: Fixed governance files and updated consistency report with (FIXED) prefix

## Roles and Owners
- **Architect Agent**: Executes fixes, validates changes, updates governance files
- **User**: Reviews proposed fixes (Manual mode), approves critical changes, validates results
- **Governance System**: Validation and compliance enforcement

## Trigger and End State
- **Trigger**: Consistency check identifies issues requiring fixes
- **End State**: All identified consistency issues resolved, schema validation passing

## Workflow Steps (65 steps)

### Phase 0. Read Architect Rules + Consistency Report
- 1. Read Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md to understand governance constraints
- 2. Read Workflow/Templates/Workflow_Template.md for workflow structure patterns
- 3. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md to understand terminology definitions
- 4. Read most recent consistency report from Logs/Architect/Consistency Review/
- 5. Parse consistency report to identify issues by severity (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW)
- 6. Store governance context and issue list for reference throughout workflow execution
- 7. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
- 8. **PRINT**: "Architect rules and consistency report loaded - {N} issues identified"

### Phase 1. Select Execution Mode
- 9. Ask user to select execution mode using popup menu:
  - **Manual**: Review and approve each fix individually (recommended for CRITICAL issues)
  - **Automatic**: Apply all non-critical fixes automatically, CRITICAL fixes require approval
- 10. Store selected execution mode for failure handling throughout workflow
- 11. **PRINT**: "Execution mode selected - [Manual/Automatic] will govern fix application"

### Phase 2. Issue Categorization and Prioritization
- 12. Categorize identified issues by type:
  - File reference issues (broken paths, missing files)
  - Terminology inconsistencies (outdated terms)
  - Workflow structure issues (missing sections, incorrect formatting)
  - Schema validation issues (categorization rule violations)
- 13. Prioritize issues by severity: CRITICAL > HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW
- 14. Group related issues for batch processing (e.g., all file reference fixes together)
- 15. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_2_complete"
- 16. **PRINT**: "Issues categorized and prioritized - {N} CRITICAL, {N} HIGH, {N} MEDIUM, {N} LOW"

### Phase 3. File Reference Fixes (CRITICAL)
- 17. **SCAN**: For each file reference issue:
  - **Manual Mode**: Present issue details and proposed fix to user via popup menu
  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply fix automatically if LOW/MEDIUM, CRITICAL requires approval
- 18. Fix Workflow_Template.md location references (update to Workflow/Templates/)
- 19. Fix missing or incorrectly named workflow files (rename or create)
- 20. Remove workflow references from rules files (architectural principle compliance)
- 21. Remove references to non-existent rules files
- 22. **VALIDATION**: Validate each fix using file existence checks
- 23. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_3_complete"
- 24. **PRINT**: "File reference fixes complete - {N} references updated"

### Phase 4. Terminology Fixes (HIGH)
- 25. **SCAN**: For each terminology inconsistency:
  - **Manual Mode**: Present term and proposed replacement via popup menu
  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply standard terminology replacements automatically
- 26. Replace outdated "gate" terminology with "validation" (excluding tool names)
- 27. Standardize agent naming conventions
- 28. Ensure consistent framework naming
- 29. **VALIDATION**: Validate terminology fixes using grep to confirm replacements
- 30. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_4_complete"
- 31. **PRINT**: "Terminology fixes complete - {N} terms standardized"

### Phase 5. Workflow Structure Fixes (MEDIUM)
- 32. **SCAN**: For each workflow structure issue:
  - **Manual Mode**: Present structure issue and proposed fix via popup menu
  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply template compliance fixes automatically
- 33. Add missing "Execution Modes" to workflow headers
- 34. Fix step numbering inconsistencies
- 35. Ensure all workflows have mandated sections (header, universal framework references)
- 36. Validate workflow follows template structure
- 37. **VALIDATION**: Validate structure fixes using template comparison
- 38. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_5_complete"
- 39. **PRINT**: "Workflow structure fixes complete - {N} workflows updated"

### Phase 6. Schema Validation Fixes (MEDIUM)
- 40. **SCAN**: For each schema validation issue:
  - **Manual Mode**: Present categorization rule violation and proposed fix via popup menu
  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply categorization rule updates automatically
- 41. Update categorization rules in Scripts/Schema/validate_schemas.py
- 42. Remove index.md exceptions if not required by architecture
- 43. Update rule files to reference correct documentation paths
- 44. **VALIDATION**: Run schema validation script to confirm all fixes
- 45. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_6_complete"
- 46. **PRINT**: "Schema validation fixes complete - validation passing"

### Phase 7. Final Validation and Report Update
- 47. Run comprehensive schema validation: `python Scripts/Schema/validate_schemas.py`
- 48. Run consistency check workflow to verify all issues resolved
- 49. Rename original consistency report with (FIXED) prefix
- 50. Generate summary of fixes applied with before/after comparison
- 51. **VALIDATION**: Validate all fixes completed successfully
- 52. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_7_complete"
- 53. **PRINT**: "Final validation complete - all consistency issues resolved"

### Phase 8. Documentation
- 54. Update AGENTS.md if agent capabilities changed during fixes
- 55. Update INDEX.md if governance structure changed
- 56. Document architectural decisions made during fix process
- 57. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_8_complete"
- 58. **PRINT**: "Documentation complete - governance files updated"

### Phase 9. Final Validation
- 59. Verify all fixes comply with Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md
- 60. Verify schema validation passes (645/645 files)
- 61. Verify no unintended changes outside target files
- 62. **VALIDATION**: Validate that final validation completed successfully
- 63. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_9_complete"
- 64. **PRINT**: "Final validation complete - architecture fully compliant"

### Phase 10. Terminate
- 65. **PRINT**: "Consistency fix workflow complete - {N} issues resolved, schema validation passing"
- 66. **TERMINATE**: End workflow execution (do not return to step 1)

---

- Place workflow file in Workflow/Architect/Architect_Consistency_Fix_Workflow.md
- Follow naming convention: {Agent}_{WorkflowType}_Workflow.md
- Check INDEX.md for folder structure compliance

 16|**Workflow Type**: Single-Execution (Utility/Tool Workflow)
 17|**Execution Modes**: Manual, Automatic
 18|
 19|## Purpose
 20|Systematic resolution of consistency issues identified by the Consistency Check Workflow. This workflow processes the consistency report and implements fixes for broken references, terminology inconsistencies, workflow structure issues, and schema validation problems. The workflow supports both Manual mode (user confirmation for each fix) and Automatic mode (batch processing of non-critical fixes).
 21|
 22|## Scope
 23|**Harness Architecture Only**: Governance files, workflows, rules, documentation (excludes /app folder)
 24|
 25|**Input**: Consistency report from Logs/Architect/Consistency Review/
 26|
 27|**Output**: Fixed governance files and updated consistency report with (FIXED) prefix
 28|
 29|## Roles and Owners
 30|- **Architect Agent**: Executes fixes, validates changes, updates governance files
 31|- **User**: Reviews proposed fixes (Manual mode), approves critical changes, validates results
 32|- **Governance System**: Validation and compliance enforcement
 33|
 34|## Trigger and End State
 35|- **Trigger**: Consistency check identifies issues requiring fixes
 36|- **End State**: All identified consistency issues resolved, schema validation passing
 37|
 38|## Workflow Steps (65 steps)
 39|
 40|### Phase 0. Read Architect Rules + Consistency Report
 41|- 1. Read Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md to understand governance constraints
 42|- 2. Read Workflow/Templates/Workflow_Template.md for workflow structure patterns
 43|- 3. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md to understand terminology definitions
 44|- 4. Read most recent consistency report from Logs/Architect/Consistency Review/
 45|- 5. Parse consistency report to identify issues by severity (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW)
 46|- 6. Store governance context and issue list for reference throughout workflow execution
 47|- 7. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
 48|- 8. **PRINT**: "Architect rules and consistency report loaded - {N} issues identified"
 49|
 50|### Phase 1. Select Execution Mode
 51|- 9. Ask user to select execution mode using popup menu:
 52|  - **Manual**: Review and approve each fix individually (recommended for CRITICAL issues)
 53|  - **Automatic**: Apply all non-critical fixes automatically, CRITICAL fixes require approval
 54|- 10. Store selected execution mode for failure handling throughout workflow
 55|- 11. **PRINT**: "Execution mode selected - [Manual/Automatic] will govern fix application"
 56|
 57|### Phase 2. Issue Categorization and Prioritization
 58|- 12. Categorize identified issues by type:
 59|  - File reference issues (broken paths, missing files)
 60|  - Terminology inconsistencies (outdated terms)
 61|  - Workflow structure issues (missing sections, incorrect formatting)
 62|  - Schema validation issues (categorization rule violations)
 63|- 13. Prioritize issues by severity: CRITICAL > HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW
 64|- 14. Group related issues for batch processing (e.g., all file reference fixes together)
 65|- 15. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_2_complete"
 66|- 16. **PRINT**: "Issues categorized and prioritized - {N} CRITICAL, {N} HIGH, {N} MEDIUM, {N} LOW"
 67|
 68|### Phase 3. File Reference Fixes (CRITICAL)
 69|- 17. **SCAN**: For each file reference issue:
 70|  - **Manual Mode**: Present issue details and proposed fix to user via popup menu
 71|  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply fix automatically if LOW/MEDIUM, CRITICAL requires approval
 72|- 18. Fix Workflow_Template.md location references (update to Workflow/Templates/)
 73|- 19. Fix missing or incorrectly named workflow files (rename or create)
 74|- 20. Remove workflow references from rules files (architectural principle compliance)
 75|- 21. Remove references to non-existent rules files
 76|- 22. **VALIDATION**: Validate each fix using file existence checks
 77|- 23. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_3_complete"
 78|- 24. **PRINT**: "File reference fixes complete - {N} references updated"
 79|
 80|### Phase 4. Terminology Fixes (HIGH)
 81|- 25. **SCAN**: For each terminology inconsistency:
 82|  - **Manual Mode**: Present term and proposed replacement via popup menu
 83|  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply standard terminology replacements automatically
 84|- 26. Replace outdated "gate" terminology with "validation" (excluding tool names)
 85|- 27. Standardize agent naming conventions
 86|- 28. Ensure consistent framework naming
 87|- 29. **VALIDATION**: Validate terminology fixes using grep to confirm replacements
 88|- 30. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_4_complete"
 89|- 31. **PRINT**: "Terminology fixes complete - {N} terms standardized"
 90|
 91|### Phase 5. Workflow Structure Fixes (MEDIUM)
 92|- 32. **SCAN**: For each workflow structure issue:
 93|  - **Manual Mode**: Present structure issue and proposed fix via popup menu
 94|  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply template compliance fixes automatically
 95|- 33. Add missing "Execution Modes" to workflow headers
 96|- 34. Fix step numbering inconsistencies
 97|- 35. Ensure all workflows have mandated sections (header, universal framework references)
 98|- 36. Validate workflow follows template structure
 99|- 37. **VALIDATION**: Validate structure fixes using template comparison
100|- 38. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_5_complete"
101|- 39. **PRINT**: "Workflow structure fixes complete - {N} workflows updated"
102|
103|### Phase 6. Schema Validation Fixes (MEDIUM)
104|- 40. **SCAN**: For each schema validation issue:
105|  - **Manual Mode**: Present categorization rule violation and proposed fix via popup menu
106|  - **Automatic Mode**: Apply categorization rule updates automatically
107|- 41. Update categorization rules in Scripts/Schema/validate_schemas.py
108|- 42. Remove index.md exceptions if not required by architecture
109|- 43. Update rule files to reference correct documentation paths
110|- 44. **VALIDATION**: Run schema validation script to confirm all fixes
111|- 45. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_6_complete"
112|- 46. **PRINT**: "Schema validation fixes complete - validation passing"
113|
114|### Phase 7. Final Validation and Report Update
115|- 47. Run comprehensive schema validation: `python Scripts/Schema/validate_schemas.py`
116|- 48. Run consistency check workflow to verify all issues resolved
117|- 49. Rename original consistency report with (FIXED) prefix
118|- 50. Generate summary of fixes applied with before/after comparison
119|- 51. **VALIDATION**: Validate all fixes completed successfully
120|- 52. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_7_complete"
121|- 53. **PRINT**: "Final validation complete - all consistency issues resolved"
122|
123|### Phase 8. Documentation
124|- 54. Update AGENTS.md if agent capabilities changed during fixes
125|- 55. Update INDEX.md if governance structure changed
126|- 56. Document architectural decisions made during fix process
127|- 57. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_8_complete"
128|- 58. **PRINT**: "Documentation complete - governance files updated"
129|
130|### Phase 9. Final Validation
131|- 59. Verify all fixes comply with Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md
132|- 60. Verify schema validation passes (645/645 files)
133|- 61. Verify no unintended changes outside target files
134|- 62. **VALIDATION**: Validate that final validation completed successfully
135|- 63. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_9_complete"
136|- 64. **PRINT**: "Final validation complete - architecture fully compliant"
137|
138|### Phase 10. Terminate
139|- 65. **PRINT**: "Consistency fix workflow complete - {N} issues resolved, schema validation passing"
140|- 66. **TERMINATE**: End workflow execution (do not return to step 1)
141|
